title: Opinion: These three ETFs have beaten S&P indexes while cutting risk
The Walt Disney Studios Posts $7.3B in Global Box Office and Record Domestic Year of $3.09 Billion
summary: The Walt Disney Studios achieved the second biggest year in industry history in 2018 with $7.3254 billion in global box office, surpassing its own previous domestic record with $3.0923 billion. Three Disney films (Avengers: Infinity War, Black Panther, and Incredibles 2) crossed the billion-dollar mark globally, and the studio released the top three industry releases domestically. Disney attributes this success to its various studios and expresses anticipation for its 2019 slate.

title: Now Hiring, With Attractive New Perk: Free College Degree
summary: Some of America's largest companies, including Walt Disney Co., Discover Financial Services, and Yum Brands Inc.'s Taco Bell, are offering free college education to their employees. This initiative reverses the traditional norm of requiring a degree before employment, with companies covering tuition, fees, and books upfront. The employers believe that the benefits of a happier and better-trained workforce outweigh the costs of funding their education.

title: Employees and Cast Members Are Changing Their Lives with Disney Aspire
summary: The Disney Aspire program is helping Walt Disney Company employees and Cast Members achieve their educational goals, covering 100% of tuition, fees, and textbooks. The article highlights success stories of participants like Anthony Payne, Leanne Morgan, and Craig J. Plummer who are advancing their careers and setting examples for their families. Valencia College recently joined the network, expanding the program's offerings and its community impact.

title: Opinion: These three ETFs have beaten S&P indexes while cutting risk
summary: This article discusses three ETFs that have outperformed S&P indexes while simultaneously reducing investment risk. The key to their success is a diversified portfolio of stocks with low price volatility. The author suggests that playing it safer can lead to enhanced long-term investment returns.

title: Netflix raised prices and the stock soared
summary: Netflix announced a price increase of 13% to 18% for its streaming service, leading to a 6.5% jump in its stock. This marks the company's largest price hike since its streaming launch and is intended to fund original content and combat competition from other streaming services. Despite previous rate increases having minimal impact on subscriber growth, Netflix's stock has traditionally benefited.

title: Netflix beats on subscriber growth, but misses slightly on revenue — stock falls after hours
summary: Netflix reported mixed fourth-quarter 2018 earnings, beating EPS estimates and subscriber additions but falling short on revenue. The company’s stock dropped after hours due to the revenue miss and lower-than-expected guidance for Q1 2019. Despite increased content spending and cash burn, Netflix saw strong international subscriber growth and plans to improve free cash flow after 2019.

title: New Zootopia-Themed Expansion Announced for Shanghai Disney Resort
summary: Shanghai Disney Resort announced its second major expansion, a new Zootopia-themed land, signifying the resort's early success and confidence in China's growing demand for themed entertainment. This expansion will feature a new major attraction, entertainment, merchandise, and food and beverage offerings, with construction targeted to begin later in 2019. The Zootopia land is expected to boost offerings, market competitiveness, and create job opportunities.

title: Netflix joins MPAA in a sign of the streaming company’s film growth
summary: Netflix has joined the Motion Picture Assn. of America, signaling its growing prominence in the film industry. This move integrates the streaming giant, which spends billions on content and recently received 15 Oscar nominations, into the lobbying group alongside traditional Hollywood studios like Disney and Universal. The MPAA, facing industry consolidation and seeking to adapt to modern viewing habits, welcomes Netflix to help advocate for storytellers and fight piracy, despite potential disagreements on film release strategies.

title: Walt Disney Co. 1st Quarter Earnings Report Shows Flat Revenue and Lower Income
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced nearly flat revenues and a 36% decrease in income for its fiscal first quarter of 2019. CEO Bob Iger highlighted the upcoming 21st Century Fox acquisition and the launch of Disney+ as top priorities. The report also detailed performance across its newly reorganized divisions, with Parks, Experiences and Consumer Products showing growth, while Direct-to-Consumer and International, and Studio Entertainment saw decreases.

title: Ron Miller, Former President and CEO of The Walt Disney Co., Dies at 85
summary: Ron Miller, former president and CEO of The Walt Disney Co. and Walt Disney's son-in-law, has died at 85. During his tenure, he was instrumental in creating Touchstone Pictures, the Disney Channel, and Epcot, and greenlit groundbreaking films like "Tron." Miller's vision aimed to broaden Disney's appeal beyond G-rated content.

title: Innovations from DisneyResearch|Studios Receive Academy’s Sci-Tech Award
summary: DisneyResearch|Studios was awarded a Technical Achievement Award by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences for its "Medusa" performance capture system. Medusa allows for highly accurate facial movement capture without markers or makeup and has been used in major blockbuster films like Star Wars and Avengers: Infinity War. The Academy also recognized Pixar co-founder Ed Catmull and his colleagues for their work on 3-D geometry representation in the film industry.

title: Big businesses promised wage hikes from Trump's tax cuts. What actually happened?
summary: This article investigates the actual impact of Trump's 2017 tax cuts on worker wages and bonuses, contrasting corporate promises with the reality. Many companies, including Emerson Electric, offered one-time bonuses or 401(k) contributions, but largely prioritized stock buybacks over sustained wage increases. The report highlights how the touted benefits for workers, like those experienced by Emerson employee Lerouise Rupert, often fell short of expectations, with significant portions of tax savings funneling into shareholder payouts instead of substantial employee compensation.

title: Trust and Pixie Dust: An HR Exec’s Disney Dream
summary: Jayne Parker, former EVP and CHRO of Walt Disney Co., discusses her career trajectory within the company and the significant HR transformations implemented during her tenure. The article highlights Disney's strategic shift to Centers of Excellence, successful talent acquisition reforms, and groundbreaking employee initiatives like Disney Aspire and CODE: Rosie, all aimed at fostering employee growth, diversity, and strategic alignment in a rapidly changing business landscape.

title: Jakks Pacific Heads to Toy Fair with New Brands, Products, and Collaborations
summary: Jakks Pacific is set to showcase an expanded lineup at Toy Fair New York, featuring new brands, product extensions, and collaborations. Highlights include additions to MorfBoard, new collectible lines Piñata Fiesta and Who’s Your Lllama, and licensed toys based on Disney Junior’s Gigantosaurus, Godzilla, Harry Potter, and Mega Man. The company will also introduce products related to its new preschool program Becca's Bunch and the Sonic the Hedgehog Pinball Track Set.

title: Disney Tops Most “Intimate” Brands Survey
summary: Disney was named the most "intimate" brand in MBLM’s Brand Intimacy 2019 Study, moving up four spots from the previous year. The study, which ranks brands based on emotional connections with consumers, found Disney resonated strongly across various demographics, especially with younger users. This recognition follows other high rankings for The Walt Disney Company in surveys like Fortune's "World’s Most Admired Companies" and Forbes' "World’s Best Employers" and "World’s Best Regarded Companies."

title: Portland family Internet monitor lands $20M
summary: Circle Media, a Portland-based company specializing in family internet monitoring, has secured $20 million in its latest funding round. This round included strategic investors with whom the company already had existing partnerships. The company's co-founders, Jelani Memory and Lance Charlish, aim to simplify the monitoring of children's online and mobile device usage.

title: How Netflix created a $1 billion arms race for TV writers
summary: Netflix has instigated a highly competitive environment for TV writers and showrunners, signing major deals worth hundreds of millions of dollars with creators like Shonda Rhimes, Ryan Murphy, and Kenya Barris. This "arms race" is driven by streaming companies building original content libraries and traditional studios consolidating, leading to immense value placed on showrunners who can create intellectual property. The article explores the motivations behind these mega-deals, their structure (often including upfront payments in lieu of residuals), and the implications for both creators and the broader entertainment industry.

title: Fox Rocked by $179M ‘Bones’ Ruling: Lying, Cheating and “Reprehensible” Studio Fraud
summary: An arbitrator has ruled against Fox in a long-running legal battle over profits from the hit show 'Bones', awarding $179 million to the show's stars and executive producer. The ruling accuses top Fox executives of lying, cheating, and committing fraud, leading to punitive damages due to the company's "reprehensible" conduct. This decision, the second-largest in TV history, could significantly impact how Hollywood studios account for profits, particularly concerning content licensing to affiliated streaming services like Hulu.

title: Ravi Ahuja Named President Business Operations & CFO For Walt Disney TV, Robert Langer Transitions To New Job
summary: Ravi Ahuja has been named President of Business Operations & CFO for Walt Disney Television following the 21st Century Fox acquisition, with Robert Langer transitioning to EVP, Finance & Planning for The Walt Disney Company. Ahuja will oversee finance, strategic planning, business development, and several other key areas, reporting to Peter Rice and Christine McCarthy. He is the latest senior executive to join Disney/ABC as part of the acquisition, having previously served as CFO for Fox Networks Group.

title: Disney is Among the Highest Ranked Companies on 2019 Axios Harris Poll 100
summary: The Walt Disney Company has been highly ranked on several prominent lists for 2019, including the Axios Harris Poll 100 where it secured the No. 5 spot for the second consecutive year. Disney also moved up to No. 3 on Reputation Institute’s Global RepTrak® 100 and was recognized by Fortune, Fast Company, MBLM, and Forbes for its corporate reputation, innovation, and brand intimacy. These accolades highlight Disney's strong public perception and performance across various corporate attributes.

title: Disney Sets March 20 Closing Date for 21st Century Fox Acquisition
summary: Disney has announced March 20 as the closing date for its $71.3 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox, marking the completion of major regulatory approvals, including from Mexico. Current 21st Century Fox shareholders have until Thursday to choose their mix of cash and Disney stock. The deal is expected to lead to industry consolidation, job reductions, and the launch of Fox Corporation from the assets not acquired by Disney.

title: Why Netflix is diving deeper into interactive storytelling
summary: Netflix is expanding its interactive storytelling initiatives following the success of Black Mirror: Bandersnatch, with plans to launch "You vs. Wild" starring Bear Grylls and explore interactive content in other genres like romance and horror. The company sees this strategy as a way to differentiate itself from increasing competition from Apple and Disney and boost viewer engagement. Netflix is also analyzing viewer behavior with Bandersnatch to refine the implementation of interactive choices in future projects.

title: Disney’s Acquisition of 21st Century Fox Will Bring an Unprecedented Collection of Content and Talent to Consumers Around the World
summary: The Walt Disney Company's acquisition of 21st Century Fox is set to become effective on March 20, 2019. This strategic move aims to expand Disney's content offerings, international footprint, and direct-to-consumer services like ESPN+, Disney+, and Hulu. The acquisition includes significant film and television production businesses from 21st Century Fox, positioning Disney as a leading global entertainment company.

title: Of Course Paul Ryan Is Taking a Job at Trump’s Favorite Company
summary: Former House Speaker Paul Ryan is joining the seven-person board of the newly formed Fox Corporation, which includes Fox News. This move comes after his retirement from Congress and is seen as a return to conservative politics and a potentially lucrative new role. The article also touches on Ryan's past criticisms and his role in the corporate tax cut that benefited companies like Fox Corp.

title: As ‘New Fox’ Stock Begins Trading, Fox News Takes Starring Role in Murdoch Empire
summary: The Fox Corporation, housing the Murdoch family's remaining assets including Fox News Channel and Fox broadcast network, began trading after the Walt Disney Company's acquisition of other 21st Century Fox parts. Fox News is positioned as the financial crown jewel of the new company, with analysts projecting it will contribute significantly to the overall earnings. Lachlan Murdoch is the chairman and CEO of the new Fox, with a focus on sports, news, and entertainment.

title: The Disney-Fox Acquisition Has Been Completed, Announces 21st Century Fox
summary: The acquisition of key entertainment assets from 21st Century Fox by The Walt Disney Company has been completed for $71.3 billion, effective March 20, 2019, at 12:02 a.m. Eastern Time. The deal consolidates major film and TV studios under Disney's umbrella and saw 21st Century Fox distribute shares of Fox Corporation as it became a standalone company. This major Hollywood deal, initially valued at $52.4 billion, concluded after regulatory approvals and a bidding war with Comcast.

title: Netflix is valued like a tech company, but its CEO just said it was a media company
summary: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings stated that the company is a media company rather than a tech company, primarily due to its significant spending on content. This stance deviates from other major tech firms that prefer to label themselves as "platforms." Hastings' comments came in response to questions about regulating tech companies, potentially allowing Netflix to avoid some scrutiny faced by its peers.

title: Former House Speaker Paul Ryan joins board of Fox News' parent company
summary: Former House Speaker Paul Ryan has been appointed to the board of directors for Fox Corp., the new parent company of Fox News and Fox Business. This appointment follows the completion of Walt Disney's purchase of 21st Century Fox, with Fox Corp. beginning public trading on Tuesday. Ryan retired from Congress earlier this year.

title: UPDATED: The Disney/21st Century Fox Merger Is Officially Complete
summary: The Disney acquisition of 21st Century Fox has been officially announced as completed, with the merger set to take effect tomorrow, March 20, 2019, at 12:02 a.m. Eastern Time. 21st Century Fox announced the distribution of Fox Corporation common stock to its stockholders, making both FOX and 21CF standalone, publicly traded companies with new stock symbols on Nasdaq.

title: New Era Dawns for Hollywood as Disney Completes $71.3B Takeover of 20th Century Fox
summary: The Walt Disney Co. completed its $71.3 billion acquisition of 20th Century Fox, marking a significant consolidation in Hollywood. This deal reduces the "Big Six" studios to five and provides Disney with extensive content for its upcoming streaming service, Disney+, as it competes with digital giants like Netflix. The acquisition is expected to lead to thousands of layoffs and raises questions about cinematic diversity and the future of risk-taking productions within the more conservative Disney structure.

title: Disney Closes $71.3 Billion Fox Deal, Creating Global Content Powerhouse
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has successfully closed its $71.3 billion acquisition of significant portions of 21st Century Fox, expanding its global content and market reach. This mega-deal adds key assets like the Fox film and TV studio, FX networks, National Geographic, Star India, and increases Disney's stake in Hulu to 60 percent, positioning the company for its upcoming Disney+ streaming service launch. The acquisition is expected to boost Disney's annual revenue and net income, despite predictions of short-term earnings drag due to integration costs and the Disney+ launch.

title: Disney Moves From Behemoth to Colossus With Closing of Fox Deal (Published 2019)
summary: The Walt Disney Company has successfully completed its $71.3 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox assets, transforming it into an unprecedented entertainment colossus. This deal significantly reshapes the media landscape, giving Disney greater leverage and allowing it to aggressively enter the streaming market with Fox content, potentially impacting competitors like Netflix and smaller studios. The acquisition includes major franchises, cable networks, and international operations, bolstering Disney's already dominant position against the backdrop of tech giants entering Hollywood.

title: Disney closes $71B US deal for Fox entertainment assets
summary: Disney has finalized its $71 billion acquisition of Fox's entertainment assets, bringing major franchises like The Simpsons, Star Wars, and Marvel's X-Men under its control. This strategic move aims to bolster Disney's upcoming streaming service, Disney Plus, enabling it to better compete with companies like Netflix and Amazon by expanding its content library. The deal also gives Disney a controlling stake in Hulu and reunites Marvel characters like the X-Men with the Avengers for future projects.

title: Disney Closes Acquisition of 21st Century Fox
summary: The Walt Disney Company has officially completed its historic $71.3 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox, creating an unprecedented collection of content and talent. This deal grants Disney ownership of major film and TV assets, including Twentieth Century Fox, FX Networks, and a 30 percent stake in Hulu, aiming to enhance Disney's direct-to-consumer strategy and global presence. Disney CEO Robert A. Iger acknowledged the challenging integration ahead but expressed confidence in the long-term value and growth opportunities.

title: Disney closes $71 billion acquisition of Twenty-First Century Fox's assets
summary: Walt Disney Co completed its $71 billion acquisition of Twenty-First Century Fox Inc's film and television assets. This deal expands Disney's content library, including franchises like X-Men and Avatar, to bolster its upcoming streaming service, Disney+. The acquisition follows a bidding war with Comcast Corp.

title: Here’s what Disney owns after the massive Disney/Fox merger
summary: The article details the implications of Disney's $71.3 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox's film and TV assets, highlighting how it reshapes the media landscape. It covers Disney's new ownership of a vast library of movies and shows, its majority stake in Hulu, and Marvel regaining access to X-Men and Fantastic Four characters, while also noting the continuation of Fox Corp as a news and sports entity. The author raises concerns about media consolidation and potential job losses stemming from the merger.

title: None of BlackBerry’s top executives work out of its Waterloo headquarters anymore
summary: BlackBerry no longer has any top executives based at its iconic Waterloo headquarters or anywhere else in Canada, with its entire executive team now operating out of Bay Area offices in California. This shift has occurred under CEO John Chen, who took over in 2013, despite BlackBerry continuing to brand itself as a Waterloo-based company and receiving Canadian government funding. While the executive presence has moved south, BlackBerry maintains a significant Canadian workforce, especially in R&D, and is still viewed as a symbol of Canadian innovation.

title: Disney Shutters Fox 2000
summary: Following its acquisition of Fox, Disney has announced the closure of the Fox 2000 label, which often produced a mix of art house films and mainstream popcorn fare. This move comes with the first wave of layoffs, including several key executives from the Fox studio system. While current projects will be completed and released, and the Fox 2000 catalog will be available on Disney's streaming services, the studio will cease to exist.

title: Viacom, AT&T reach deal that keeps Nickelodeon, MTV and Comedy Central on DirecTV
summary: Viacom and AT&T reached a new distribution agreement, preventing a blackout of Viacom's channels like Nickelodeon, MTV, and Comedy Central on AT&T's DirecTV service. The deal was struck after tense negotiations, reportedly involving fee reductions from Viacom's side, as AT&T, heavily in debt, sought to cut costs. This resolution avoids a significant disruption for 24.5 million AT&T TV subscribers and addresses concerns from both companies facing industry shifts and subscriber challenges.

title: Disney Earns Perfect Score for LGBTQ Workplace Equality
summary: The Walt Disney Company achieved a perfect score of 100 on the 2019 Corporate Equality Index (CEI) for LGBTQ workplace equality, marking its 13th consecutive year of top marks. Administered by the Human Rights Campaign Foundation, the CEI evaluates corporate policies and practices, recognizing Disney as a "Best Place to Work for LGBTQ Equality." Disney's commitment includes comprehensive benefits, support for transitioning employees, LGBTQ business employee resource groups, and contributions to diverse organizations.

title: How Netflix plans on owning your kids’ screen time
summary: Netflix is heavily investing in children's animation, spending an estimated $1.1 billion this year, to appeal to its broad global subscriber base and fend off competition. Unlike traditional studios, Netflix aims for a diverse range of content without a singular "brand" to cater to every household member's viewing preferences. The company is encouraging creators to pursue unique visions and is experimenting with new interactive features to engage young viewers.

title: How Lachlan Murdoch Went From Studying Philosophy at Princeton to Exploiting White Nationalism at Fox News
summary: This article traces Lachlan Murdoch's journey from a philosophy student at Princeton, where he wrote a thesis on morality, to his current role overseeing Fox News, which the author contends exploits white nationalism. It explores his upbringing, his conservative leanings, and the family dynamics, including his brief departure from his father's business and the succession struggle among the Murdoch children, culminating in Lachlan's ascent to leadership. The piece contrasts his early intellectual pursuits with his later actions as a media proprietor, suggesting a transformation shaped by his relationship with his powerful father.

title: Chart: Everything That Disney Owns
summary: This article details the extensive list of companies, brands, and franchises owned by The Walt Disney Company following its acquisition of significant parts of 21st Century Fox. It highlights key acquisitions like Fox Family, Fox Animation, and Fox Networks, alongside existing properties such as Marvel, Lucasfilm, ESPN, and Pixar. The article also mentions Disney's major competitors in the media landscape.

title: ‘Captain Marvel’ Crosses $1 Billion Worldwide
summary: Captain Marvel has crossed the $1 billion mark globally, becoming the seventh Marvel Studios film to achieve this milestone. The movie earned $358 million domestically and $645 million internationally as of April 2, 2019, with a strong opening weekend of $153 million in the U.S. and a $455 million global debut. This success contributes to the Marvel Cinematic Universe's collective box office earnings of over $18.5 billion.

title: How Rupert Murdoch’s Empire of Influence Remade the World (Published 2019)
summary: This article details Rupert Murdoch's vast media empire and its significant influence on politics and world affairs across continents. It explores the family dynamics, particularly the rivalry between his sons Lachlan and James for succession, and Murdoch's strategic use of his media outlets to shape political outcomes, including the rise of Donald Trump and Brexit. The piece highlights Murdoch's consistent push for right-wing ideologies and his transactional relationships with political leaders over decades.

title: 'Treated as cheap labor': Disney underpays women, lawsuit alleges
summary: The Walt Disney Company is facing a class-action lawsuit alleging systematic underpayment of women and "widespread" discrimination. The lawsuit comes just after Disney's acquisition of 21st Century Fox and follows a report that the company pays men 22% more on average than women in the UK. Two longtime female employees, LaRonda Rasmussen and Karen Moore, allege significant pay disparities compared to male counterparts despite similar roles and experience.

title: Disney Spotlights Comprehensive Direct-to-Consumer Strategy at 2019 Investor Day
summary: The Walt Disney Company's Investor Day showcased its comprehensive direct-to-consumer strategy, highlighting Disney+, Hulu, Hotstar, and ESPN+. Disney+ is set to launch on November 12, 2019, at $6.99 a month, featuring content from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and National Geographic, including original series and films. The company detailed a robust content slate and global expansion plans, aiming to deliver significant value to consumers and shareholders.

title: Disney CEO Robert Iger announces 2021 retirement
summary: Walt Disney CEO Robert Iger announced his plan to step down from his role when his current contract expires at the end of 2021. Iger, who became CEO in 2005, has previously extended his tenure but stated that 2021 will be his time to finally depart, following the company's significant acquisitions like Pixar, Marvel, and Lucasfilm. The 2021 extension was contingent on the successful $71.3-billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox's entertainment assets.

title: Every Amazing Announcement About Disney+ from The Walt Disney Company’s 2019 Investor Day
summary: The Walt Disney Company's 2019 Investor Day revealed details about the Disney+ streaming service, launching in the U.S. on November 12, 2019, priced at $6.99 a month. The service will feature over 25 original series and 10 original films from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and National Geographic, alongside classic titles and all 30 seasons of The Simpsons. Key executives presented the extensive content slate, emphasizing the company's direct connection to consumers.

title: Live Blog: The Walt Disney Company Investor Day 2019 — Disney+ Reveal and More
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced an Investor Day event to unveil details about its upcoming streaming services, particularly Disney+. The event was scheduled to begin at 2 p.m. PDT/5 p.m. EDT, with a live blog covering all emerging news from the special presentation. Key topics expected included Disney+, ESPN, Hotstar, and Hulu.

title: Netflix’s Market Value Dropped $8 Billion After the Disney Plus Announcement
summary: Netflix Inc. experienced an $8 billion drop in market capitalization after Disney announced its new, cheaper streaming service, Disney+, slated to launch in November. Disney's stock, conversely, surged to a record high, adding $25 billion in market value, as the company detailed its content-rich streaming offering designed to compete directly with Netflix.

title: Disney CEO Bob Iger lays out details on company's Netflix competitor
summary: Disney CEO Bob Iger discussed the company's new streaming platform, Disney+, and its position against competitors like Netflix during an interview with CNBC's David Faber. The discussion also touched upon impending job cuts resulting from consolidation efforts. The interview followed Disney's investor day, providing insights into their strategy moving forward.

title: Netflix Just Dropped $8 Billion in Market Value on Disney+ News
summary: Netflix Inc. experienced an $8 billion drop in market capitalization following Walt Disney Co.'s announcement of its new, cheaper streaming service, Disney+. Disney+ is set to launch on November 12 at a price point significantly lower than Netflix's most popular U.S. plan, causing investor concern for Netflix.

title: Marcella Regniault
summary: Marcella Regniault is the Vice President, Digital Sales Planning and Client Services at ESPN, where she oversees digital client services strategy to optimize advertising inventory and revenue. Before joining ESPN, she held significant roles at JP Morgan Chase Inc., focusing on ad operations, and at Ziff Davis, managing marketing and sales operations. Her extensive career also includes leadership positions at TVGuide.com, The Wall Street Journal Digital Network, and Time, Inc.

title: Hulu buys AT&T’s stake for $1.43 billion
summary: Hulu has repurchased AT&T's nearly 10% equity stake for $1.43 billion, valuing the streaming service at $15 billion. This transaction positions AT&T to focus on its own WarnerMedia streaming service, while Disney solidifies its control over Hulu with a 60% stake. Hulu aims for profitability by fiscal year 2023 or 2024, despite an anticipated $1.5 billion operating loss in fiscal year 2019.

title: AT&T sells Hulu stake in deal that values streaming service at $15 billion
summary: AT&T has sold its minority stake in Hulu back to the streaming service, a deal that valued Hulu at $15 billion. AT&T's 9.5% interest was valued at $1.43 billion, and the company plans to use the sales proceeds to pay down debt. Hulu's CEO expressed gratitude for AT&T's support.

title: With Disney in Control, Hulu Buys Out AT&T Stake for $1.4 Billion
summary: Hulu, now majority-controlled by Disney, has bought out AT&T Inc.'s 9.5 percent stake for approximately $1.43 billion. This deal values Hulu at $15 billion and leaves Walt Disney Co. and Comcast Corp. as the sole owners of the streaming service. Disney gained majority control last month after acquiring Fox assets.

title: Hulu Buys AT&T’s Minority Stake in Joint Venture
summary: AT&T has sold its 9.5% minority stake in Hulu back to the streaming video joint venture for $1.43 billion, valuing Hulu at $15 billion. The transaction was signed and closed simultaneously without needing third-party approvals. AT&T plans to use the proceeds to reduce its debt.

title: Walt Disney in control, Hulu buys out AT&T for $1.4 billion
summary: Hulu has bought out AT&T's 9.5% stake for about $1.43 billion, valuing the company at $15 billion, leaving Walt Disney Co. and Comcast Corp. as the sole owners. Disney, which now has majority control, is considering an international rollout for Hulu, which is projected to lose $1.5 billion this year but aims for profitability by FY23 or FY24. AT&T plans to use the proceeds to reduce its substantial debt load.

title: Texas Children’s and Disney partnership brings the magic of the mouse to patients
summary: Texas Children’s Hospital and The Walt Disney Co. have launched a pilot program called Disney Team of Heroes, bringing the magic of Disney to hospitalized children. This initiative aims to create "moments of joy" and provide delightful distractions through Disney-themed murals, hospital gowns, play spaces, mobile movie theaters, and an app. The partnership seeks to enhance patient experiences and may expand to other children's hospitals globally.

title: Netflix is opening a production hub in NYC
summary: Netflix is expanding its presence in New York City by opening a new production hub, which is expected to create hundreds of jobs and involve up to $100 million in investments. This move follows Amazon backing out of Long Island City and comes as Netflix faces increased competition from other streaming services like Disney, demonstrating its strategy to grow beyond Hollywood. The state of New York is offering Netflix up to $4 million in performance-based tax incentives for job creation.

title: Opinion | Abigail Disney: It's time to call out my family's company — and anyone else rich off their workers' backs
summary: Abigail Disney, president of Fork Films and co-founder of Level Forward, addresses wage inequality at The Walt Disney Co. She contends that the Disney brand holds a unique place in the economic landscape due to its reliance on emotion and sentiment, suggesting it has the potential to lead the way in humane business practices if its leaders chose to do so. She emphasizes that her comments are personal views and not representative of her family.

title: Disney heiress calls CEO Bob Iger’s $65 million pay package ‘insane’
summary: Disney heiress Abigail Disney criticized CEO Bob Iger's $65.6 million pay package as "insane," highlighting the vast disparity between his salary and that of the median Disney employee. She advocated for significant pay raises for the company's lowest-paid workers, arguing that Disney's profitability leaves no excuse not to do so.

title: Abigail Disney Urges Walt Disney Co. to “Lead” in Op-Ed About Wage Inequality
summary: Abigail Disney, great-niece of Walt Disney, published an op-ed in The Washington Post criticizing wage inequality at The Walt Disney Co., specifically highlighting CEO Bob Iger's "insane" 2018 compensation of over $65 million. She urges the company to lead in improving employee wages and promoting a more humane way of doing business, contrasting CEO pay growth with minimal worker pay increases. Disney also criticized the company's $3.6 billion share buyback, arguing it dwarfed employee raises and primarily enriched shareholders.

title: Variety, iHeartMedia Launch New Film Podcast ‘The Big Ticket’ With Marc Malkin
summary: Variety and iHeartMedia have launched a new weekly film-focused podcast called "The Big Ticket," hosted by Marc Malkin. The podcast will feature interviews with Hollywood stars and filmmakers, with its debut episodes focusing on "Avengers: Endgame" and upcoming guests including Halle Berry and Keanu Reeves. This partnership aims to expand the reach of Variety's journalism to wider audiences through iHeartMedia's platforms.

title: Disney heir calls on company to give 50% of exec bonuses to lowest-paid employees
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of co-founder Roy Disney, is advocating for Disney to dedicate 50% of executive bonuses to its lowest-paid employees. She points out the significant disparity between executive compensation, such as CEO Bob Iger's $66 million pay package, and the median employee salary of $46,127, arguing that a portion of executive bonuses could significantly benefit lower-paid workers without impacting executives' quality of life. The company, Disney (DIS), has responded by highlighting its investments in employee wages and benefits, and defending Iger's performance-based pay.

title: Disney heiress calls out wage inequality at Walt Disney Company
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of Roy Disney, publicly criticized wage inequality at the Walt Disney Company, highlighting that CEO Bob Iger's 2018 compensation was 1,424 times the median worker's pay. She urged executives to donate 50% of their bonuses to the lowest-paid employees to address the widening gap between top management and the average worker. Disney argued that despite a $1,000 bonus to some employees, the company prioritized stock buybacks over significant worker compensation improvements.

title: Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Makes History with $1.2 Billion Global Debut
summary: Marvel Studios' Avengers: Endgame set a new global box office record with an unprecedented $1.209 billion debut, becoming the first film to surpass $1 billion in its opening weekend. The film achieved this milestone in just five days and broke numerous domestic and international records, including an estimated $350 million domestically and $859 million internationally. This monumental success solidifies the Marvel Cinematic Universe's dominance, with critical acclaim and significant contributions to The Walt Disney Studios' financial performance.

title: Disney and Make-A-Wish Launch #FriendLikeMe Challenge in Celebration of ‘Aladdin’
summary: The Walt Disney Company and Make-A-Wish have launched the #FriendLikeMe Challenge in celebration of the new Aladdin movie, starring Will Smith. For every public social media post with #FriendLikeMe through May 24, 2019, Disney will donate $5, up to $1 million, to Make-A-Wish to help grant wishes for children with critical illnesses. This initiative highlights the long-standing collaboration between Disney and Make-A-Wish, which has granted over 130,000 wishes since 1980.

title: Disney Touches Record High as ‘Endgame’ Dominates Box Office
summary: Walt Disney Co. shares reached record levels after its film "Avengers: Endgame" shattered box-office records. The film's success is expected to significantly boost the studio division's contribution to overall profit and is seen as a positive indicator ahead of the Disney+ streaming service launch. Analysts also anticipate upside for theater companies due to the film's performance.

title: Vice Media Gets $250 Million in Debt Funding From George Soros, Other Investors
summary: Vice Media has secured $250 million in debt funding from an investment consortium including George Soros, led by 23 Capital, to revitalize its business. This capital infusion is intended to accelerate Vice's growth plans and execute the strategic vision of CEO Nancy Dubuc, who aims for profitability within the next fiscal year. The funding comes after a period of revenue shortfalls, employee layoffs, and a significant drop in the company's valuation.

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ is Fastest Ever to $2 Billion
summary: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ achieved a historic milestone by crossing $2 billion at the global box office in just 11 days, becoming the fastest film to reach this threshold. It is now the second highest-grossing film of all time, surpassing "Avengers: Infinity War," "Star Wars: The Force Awakens," and "Titanic." The film also set numerous international records, including becoming the highest-grossing non-local film in China and the highest-grossing Hollywood film in India, among other territories.

title: Target rebrands digital-advertising business as Roundel
summary: Target has rebranded its digital advertising business from Target Media Network to Roundel, signaling an aggressive push into the digital advertising sector. The company aims to leverage its customer data and "exceptional branding" to offer personalized ad campaigns for its 1,000 clients, including major brands like Disney and Coca-Cola. This move positions Target to compete more directly with other retailers like Amazon and Walmart, which have also seen success in their advertising businesses.

title: Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Endgame Sets New Record for IMAX China’s Highest-grossing Title Ever With 496 Million Rmb
summary: Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Endgame has become IMAX China’s all-time highest-grossing title in just 12 days, reaching approximately RMB 496 million. The film nearly doubled the entire run of Avengers: Infinity War in IMAX China and set multiple records, including the best midnight, opening day, three-day opening, and biggest opening week for IMAX in China. IMAX contributed nearly 13% of the film’s overall gross in China from only 1% of the total screens, highlighting the success of the film shot entirely with IMAX cameras.

title: Fox Corp. Won’t Reunite With News Corp, CEO Lachlan Murdoch Says
summary: Fox Corp. CEO Lachlan Murdoch stated at an investor day that the company will not reunite with News Corp, despite speculation after its split from Fox entertainment assets. He emphasized that the new Fox Corporation, focusing on news, entertainment, and sports, will pursue growth through deals that align closely with its core businesses and expertise. The company also recently adopted a "poison pill" to protect against hostile takeover attempts, clarifying it's not intended to block board-approved transactions.

title: How DisneyResearch|Studios’ Technology and Industrial Light & Magic Artistry Helped Reinvent Hulk in Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’
summary: This article details how DisneyResearch|Studios (DRS) technology, Anyma, and Industrial Light & Magic (ILM) artistry were crucial in reinventing the Hulk for Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’. Anyma, an advanced motion capture system, allowed for the nuanced performance of Mark Ruffalo to be captured and translated to the character, enabling the depiction of a merged Banner-Hulk entity. This collaboration highlights a long-term strategy for technological innovation within Disney to enhance film production.

title: Netflix Acquires Children’s Education Company StoryBots
summary: Netflix has acquired StoryBots, a children's media content brand founded by the creators of JibJab. The acquisition aims to expand Netflix's children's programming and establish StoryBots as a global educational entertainment brand, leveraging Netflix's scale for distribution, merchandising, and licensing. The deal terms were undisclosed, but Netflix stated they were "immaterial," and the StoryBots founders will continue to work within Netflix's animation department.

title: Safety-sense with Spider-Man™: United Airlines Launches New Safety Video Featuring Superhero
summary: United Airlines is launching a new inflight safety video featuring Spider-Man as part of a broader promotional partnership with Sony Pictures for the movie Spider-Man™: Far From Home. The collaboration will also include Spider-Man-themed Polaris business class amenity kits and MileagePlus Exclusives experiences. The video aims to engage customers with an entertaining mini-drama while emphasizing United's commitment to safety.

title: NBC is expected to take Netflix favorite ‘The Office’ to its new streaming service
summary: NBCUniversal is strongly hinting that "The Office," currently a popular Netflix favorite, will be moving to its new, as-yet-unnamed streaming service launching in mid-2020. This move is seen as NBCU's strategy to take control of its valuable properties and a potentially significant blow to Netflix, which saw "The Office" streamed for 52 million minutes in 2018. The new NBCU service will be ad-supported, and the company is actively seeking sponsors for its launch.

title: Disney to buy full control of Hulu from NBC owner Comcast
summary: Disney is taking full operational control of the streaming service Hulu from Comcast in a deal that values Hulu at $27.5 billion U.S. This move positions Disney to better compete with Netflix, especially as Disney prepares to launch its own streaming service, Disney+. The agreement allows Disney to acquire Comcast's remaining 33 percent stake after January 2024.

title: Communication Services XLC ETF Closes Up 2.24%
summary: The Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) closed up 2.24% on Wednesday, amidst a strong market performance and news of delayed automotive tariffs. The XLC ETF, composed of major communication services companies like Facebook, Google, and Netflix, represents a relatively new sector formed in late 2018. The sector's constituents include significant growth drivers, though some analysts express caution about potential over-regulation.

title: Eleven New Disney Legends to Be Honored During D23 Expo 2019
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that 11 new individuals will be honored with the Disney Legends Award during the D23 Expo 2019. The honorees include Robert Downey Jr., Jon Favreau, James Earl Jones, Bette Midler, Kenny Ortega, Ming-Na Wen, and Hans Zimmer, recognized for their significant contributions across film, television, and theme parks. The awards ceremony will be hosted by Disney Chairman and CEO Bob Iger and will involve a handprint ceremony for the recipients.

title: Jefferies Financial has highest-paid CEO among NY companies
summary: Richard Handler, CEO of Jefferies Financial Group, was the highest-paid CEO among New York-based companies, earning $44.7 million in 2018, a 105% increase from the previous year. His compensation included a $26 million stock award and $18.7 million in base pay. This places him fourth overall on The Wall Street Journal's list of highest-paid S&P 500 CEOs, despite a general trend of falling shareholder returns.

title: Lions Gate offered to sell Starz to CBS for $5.5 billion - sources
summary: Lions Gate Entertainment reportedly offered to sell its cable channel Starz to CBS Corp for $5.5 billion, after previously rejecting an informal $5 billion bid from CBS. This move highlights CBS's ambition to compete more aggressively in the media landscape, potentially ahead of merger discussions with Viacom Inc. The news led to a rise in Lions Gate shares and a marginal decline for CBS shares.

title: New Coke Was a Debacle. It’s Coming Back. Blame ‘Stranger Things.’ (Published 2019)
summary: New Coke, the famously failed soft drink from 1985, is making a limited-time comeback due to a promotional partnership with Netflix's "Stranger Things." The vintage beverage will be available starting Thursday and will appear in the show's upcoming third season, which is set in summer 1985. This collaboration is part of Netflix's broader strategy to ramp up corporate partnerships and merchandising to attract new subscribers and generate revenue without commercials.

title: Coca-Cola Will Revive New Coke in Alliance With Netflix, ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Coca-Cola is reviving New Coke for a limited time as part of a partnership with Netflix, integrating the infamous beverage into the third season of "Stranger Things," which is set in 1985. This marketing initiative aims to promote both the return of the series and gives Coca-Cola a unique way to connect with streaming audiences, despite New Coke's historical marketing failure. Coca-Cola will make 500,000 cans available online and in select locations, also releasing limited-edition original Coke with "Stranger Things" designs.

title: Coca-Cola is bringing back New Coke in honor of ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Coca-Cola is bringing back a limited number of New Coke cans as a promotion for the third season of "Stranger Things," which is set in 1985 when New Coke originally debuted and famously flopped. This partnership with Netflix allows Coca-Cola to engage with consumers in changing media landscapes and aims to "break the internet" with the nostalgic product, which will be available through various promotional channels. Netflix is also partnering with several other companies for show promotion, leveraging physical products to reach wider audiences.

title: Walt Disney CEO Bob Iger Says It's “Very Difficult” To Do Georgia Business With New Abortion Law
summary: Walt Disney CEO Bob Iger stated it would be "very difficult" for the company to continue doing business in Georgia if the new "heartbeat" abortion law takes effect. He expressed doubts about continued filming in the state, citing potential reluctance from employees to work there. This sentiment echoes concerns from other companies like Netflix, despite Georgia's significant tax credits and film production industry.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge is Dedicated at Disneyland Park
summary: Disneyland Park officially dedicated Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge, the largest single-themed land expansion in Disney Parks history, with a grand opening ceremony attended by Disney CEO Bob Iger, George Lucas, and Skywalker Saga actors. The new land, opening to guests tomorrow, offers immersive experiences including two attractions, advanced technology integrated with the Play Disney Parks mobile app, and unique retail and culinary adventures designed to deepen guest engagement with the Star Wars universe. Walt Disney Imagineering and Lucasfilm collaborated extensively to ensure authenticity and realism, redefining the Disney park experience by allowing guests to become active participants in the Star Wars galaxy.

title: SETTING THE STAGE
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of film and television production in Los Angeles, driven by streaming services and tax incentives, which has led to a boom for soundstage owners. It highlights that studio spaces are near 100% occupancy, making it a lucrative but operationally intensive business for property owners. Key players like Hudson Pacific Properties, Occidental Entertainment Group, and Hackman Capital are expanding their soundstage portfolios, with long-term leases becoming more common due to high demand.

title: 'Merch by Amazon' t-shirt business increasing orders from Disney to Dr. Seuss
summary: Amazon's 'Merch by Amazon' on-demand t-shirt printing service is increasingly being used by major entertainment companies like Walt Disney Co and Dr. Seuss. This service allows brands to produce merchandise closer to the point of sale, eliminating the need for large upfront inventory commitments and traditional supply chains. The trend is contributing to Amazon's growing influence in the clothing industry and allows for more niche and timely product offerings.

title: How to watch the 2019 NBA Finals live on ABC or TSN without cable
summary: This article provides a guide for cord-cutters in the United States and Canada looking to stream the 2019 NBA Finals live. It outlines various options for watching ABC's coverage in the U.S. and TSN's coverage in Canada, including free over-the-air broadcasts and paid streaming services. The article also lists the schedule for the remaining games between the Golden State Warriors and the Toronto Raptors.

title: Is a construction company right in suing a cafe over the word cat?
summary: Caterpillar, the multi-billion dollar construction equipment giant, has filed a cease-and-desist order against a small Santa Cruz coffee shop, Cat & Cloud Coffee, for using the word "Cat" on its apparel. The article questions the company's decision, comparing it to Disney's inaction against a small dry-cleaning business using a Disney character, and highlights the public and the coffee shop's frustration. It suggests that such disputes often come down to economic sense rather than who is "right or wrong."

title: Clorox Brand Has a (Toy) Story to Tell
summary: The Clorox brand has partnered with Disney and Pixar for a co-branded marketing campaign tied to "Toy Story 4," leveraging the film's theme of new adventures and messes. This collaboration is their most robust to date, featuring a national TV commercial, in-store promotions, a sweepstakes, and discounted movie tickets. The partnership aims to keep Clorox relevant and maintain its leadership in the cleaning category during a typically quiet merchandising period.

title: Joe Quenqua Joins WW as Chief Communications Officer
summary: WW (NASDAQ: WW), formerly Weight Watchers, announced that Joe Quenqua will join the company as Chief Communications Officer, effective June 10, 2019. Quenqua, a former Disney executive, will lead global communications, leveraging his thirty years of experience in brand building and strategic corporate communications to shape WW's story as it evolves into a global wellness partner. He will focus on enhancing the ambassador program, community activations, and promoting the WW App.

title: Building a Simple, Low Cost Indexed ETF Portfolio in USD
summary: This article discusses the advantages of building a low-cost, indexed ETF portfolio using USD-denominated ETFs, primarily to reduce withholding taxes in registered accounts like RRSPs. It explains the concept of withholding taxes on ETFs, strategies to efficiently convert CAD to USD using Norbert's Gambit, and outlines several USD ETF portfolio options with significantly lower total MERs compared to their CAD counterparts. The author emphasizes the potential savings, especially for larger portfolios, despite the initial effort involved in currency conversion and managing US-listed ETFs.

title: Amazon pulls back from original kids programming
summary: Amazon Studios is reportedly scaling back its investment in original animated shows for young children, shifting its focus to content for families to view together and for young adult audiences. This strategic change comes amidst executive changes and internal debates over the value of kids' programming in driving Prime memberships, especially as competitors like Netflix, Disney, and Apple continue to invest heavily in the children's content space. The company will continue to produce existing kids' animated series but will prioritize licensing kids' content and developing more mature animation, including young adult animated series.

title: Lions Gate studio struggles amid Hollywood behemoths
summary: Lions Gate Entertainment Corp. is facing significant challenges, with its market value halved over the last year as it struggles to produce new blockbusters and compete with larger, merged entertainment companies. The 22-year-old studio is exploring various strategic options, including acquisition, selling off assets like Starz, or attempting to scale up to maintain relevance in Hollywood's evolving landscape. The article highlights that Lions Gate stock is trading at around $12, significantly lower than a previous $41 per share offer from Hasbro, and analysts suggest the company could be worth more in a breakup scenario.

title: FuboTV Launches Fubo Sports Network, a Free Streaming Service
summary: FuboTV is launching Fubo Sports Network, a free streaming service offering live sports event coverage, news, and exclusive programming, targeting widespread distribution beyond its own platform. Initially featuring recycled content, the network aims for brand awareness, subscriber acquisition for its premium bundles, and $5 million in incremental ad revenue in its first year. The move comes as FuboTV faces strong competition in the over-the-top TV market and recently increased its subscription prices.

title: Lion King Collection Roars into Build-A-Bear Workshop
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop has launched a new collection of Disney The Lion King furry friends, outfits, and accessories, coinciding with the release of the new movie adaptation. The collection, available in stores and online, includes characters like Young Nala, Young Simba, Nala, Simba, Pumbaa, and Timon, with optional sound chips and accessories. Special in-store activities, photo opportunities, and movie premiere weekend events are planned for July and August.

title: Sempra Energy Names Brian L. Kelly Vice President Of Federal Government Affairs
summary: Sempra Energy announced the appointment of Brian L. Kelly as Vice President of Federal Government Affairs, effective July 8, 2019. Kelly, based in Washington, D.C., will lead the company's federal legislative and regulatory priorities, succeeding Maryam Sabbaghian Brown. He brings extensive experience in public policy and government affairs from his previous roles, including founder of BK Strategies and senior director at America's Natural Gas Alliance.

title: Liberty Media CFO Mark Carleton to Retire
summary: Liberty Media announced that CFO Mark Carleton has retired but will remain with the company as a senior advisor. Brian Wendling, formerly controller, has been named principal financial officer, while other executive roles were also adjusted. Liberty Media, controlled by John Malone, owns stakes in SiriusXM Satellite Radio, the Atlanta Braves, Formula One, and other prominent companies.

title: ‘Friends’ to Move to HBO Max, WarnerMedia’s New Streaming Service
summary: WarnerMedia's new streaming service, HBO Max, will become the exclusive streaming home for the classic sitcom "Friends." Launching next spring following a limited release, HBO Max will also feature original content from stars like Nicole Kidman, Reese Witherspoon, and Anna Kendrick, as WarnerMedia aims to compete with industry leader Netflix. This move is part of the broader trend of major media companies entering the streaming-video market with their own well-known TV and movie brands.

title: SUNBRELLA® EXTENDS PARTNERSHIP THROUGH 2026, INTRODUCES NEW FAN VENUE
summary: Sunbrella® has extended its partnership with the Wyndham Championship through the 2026 tournament, continuing its role as a platinum partner and official volunteer partner. As part of this extension, Sunbrella® will debut the new Sunbrella® Wine Deck, a fan amenity on the 17th fairway, and will also bring back the Sunbrella® Comfort Zone. This collaboration highlights Sunbrella's commitment to enhancing the fan experience and supporting event volunteers.

title: Disney Content Sales President Janice Marinelli to Depart
summary: Janice Marinelli, President of global sales and marketing at Walt Disney’s direct-to-consumer and international segment, announced her departure after a 34-year career. She cited the integration of 21st Century Fox and the rapid industry changes as factors in her decision. Marinelli oversaw significant operations including the distribution of Disney's film and TV programming and spearheaded the development of Movies Anywhere.

title: Netflix stock drops more than 10 percent after earnings shortfall
summary: Netflix Inc.'s shares plunged after reporting a loss of U.S. customers and significantly slower international growth, missing analyst expectations. This shortfall, the first since 2011, raises investor concerns about heavy program spending and low profitability amidst looming competition from new streaming services by Disney and Apple.

title: Louis Vuitton Owner Bernard Arnault Replaces Microsoft’s Bill Gates as World’s 2nd Richest Person
summary: Bernard Arnault, owner of Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy (LVMH), has surpassed Bill Gates to become the world's second-richest person according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Arnault's net worth rose to US$107.6 billion due to a US$39 billion gain in 2019 alone, pushing Gates to the third position. This shift highlights the significant wealth accumulation of top billionaires.

title: Disney company blasts Abigail Disney's 'stunt' park visit
summary: The Walt Disney Company has issued a strong response to comments made by Disney heiress Abigail Disney after her visit to Disneyland to investigate worker conditions. Abigail Disney claimed workers were struggling to afford food, while the company labeled her visit a "stunt" and called her comments "baseless" and "egregious." Disney asserted that it pays its workers an average of $19.50 an hour, with a starting wage of $15.

title: Netflix Loses $17 Billion in Value in One Day
summary: Netflix's market value dropped by $17 billion in a single day after the company announced it added only 2.7 million subscribers in the most recent quarter, significantly missing its 5 million forecast. This subscriber miss, particularly a loss of U.S. subscribers for the first time, led to a 10 percent stock price drop and sparked concerns among analysts about future growth, especially with new competition from Disney and WarnerMedia on the horizon. Despite some bullish outlooks focusing on long-term potential, many analysts are re-evaluating Netflix's valuation and growth strategy.

title: FOX NFL Thursday Adds Another Hall of Famer to Star-Studded Lineup
summary: Tony Gonzalez, Class of 2019 Pro Football Hall of Famer, is joining the FOX NFL THURSDAY pregame show for the NFL's 100th season, starting September 26th. He will appear regularly alongside Michael Strahan, Terry Bradshaw, and Howie Long, with Strahan hosting the show. FOX Thursday Night Football games will be available on Amazon Prime Video, Twitch, and various NFL and FOX digital properties.

title: Netflix is not a tech company
summary: Benedict Evans argues that Netflix, despite its reliance on technology, is fundamentally a TV company, much like Sky was in its time. He uses "technology as a crowbar" as a metaphor to explain how companies leverage tech to disrupt traditional industries, but their core business remains within that industry. The article emphasizes that for Netflix, the critical questions are "TV questions" related to content, rights, and industry dynamics, rather than "tech questions" typical of Silicon Valley.

title: LendingTree embroiled in legal dispute with a subsidiary over $40 million dividend
summary: LendingTree is entangled in a legal dispute with its bankrupt subsidiary, Home Loan Center Inc., over a $40 million dividend authorized by LendingTree CEO Doug Lebda. Home Loan Center claims the transfer was fraudulent as it was dissolving and had outstanding debts, leading to allegations of Lebda breaching his fiduciary duty. LendingTree disputes the claims but has begun settlement talks, while stating it will vigorously contest the allegations if no settlement is reached.

title: Mike Morrison
summary: Mike Morrison is the Vice President of ESPN BET and ESPN Fantasy, responsible for leading the sports betting business for ESPN. He previously held roles as Vice President, Business Development, and spent a decade leading ESPN’s businesses in Asia Pacific, overseeing digital media development and commercial operations. Morrison joined ESPN in 2007 through an acquisition and started his career in radio and television news.

title: Former Paramount, Warner Bros. Exec Tom Lesinski Named CEO of National CineMedia
summary: Tom Lesinski, a former executive at Paramount, Warner Bros., and Legendary Entertainment, has been appointed CEO of National CineMedia, an in-theater advertising firm. Lesinski previously served as chairman of the company's board since August 2018 and brings extensive experience in entertainment, digital media, sales, marketing, and advertising. His appointment follows AMC Entertainment's sale of its remaining stake in National CineMedia to Cinemark Holdings and Cineworld Group for $156.8 million in 2018.

title: Netflix Global Real Estate Grab: How the Streamer Is Expanding From London to Singapore
summary: Netflix is rapidly expanding its physical presence globally through significant investments in studio facilities and high-end office spaces. The company has acquired or leased properties in major cities worldwide, including Toronto, London, Mexico City, New York, Mumbai, Singapore, and Seoul, to support its booming content production and growing employee base. This expansion reflects a strategic move to establish localized hubs for content creation and corporate operations.

title: Global firms are sounding the alarm as escalating Hong Kong protests deal a 'serious blow' to the city's outlook
summary: Global firms are increasingly warning about the negative impact of escalating Hong Kong protests on their business outlooks, with many already experiencing lost revenue and deterred investment. The protests have caused significant disruptions, particularly in retail, luxury goods, airlines, and the hotel industry, impacting sales, tourist traffic, and occupancy rates. Financial institutions are also concerned about potential capital flight and a "serious blow" to Hong Kong's long-term competitiveness as an international financial center.

title: Disney Publishing Worldwide and Disney+ Announce ‘One Day at Disney’
summary: Disney Publishing Worldwide and Disney+ announced "One Day at Disney," a collaborative project featuring a 224-page coffee table book and a 52-episode short-form documentary series. Debuting on December 3, the project will highlight the creative forces behind The Walt Disney Company through stories and images of employees and cast members globally, from Disneyland to Pixar. A feature-length documentary will kick off the series, profiling diverse individuals across various Disney roles.

title: Disney Legends Awards Ceremony Kicks Off Exciting D23 Expo 2019
summary: The Walt Disney Company held its 32nd annual Disney Legends Awards ceremony at D23 Expo 2019, honoring 12 individuals including Robert Downey Jr., Jon Favreau, Bette Midler, and Robin Roberts for their significant contributions to the Disney legacy. The expo also provided a preview of the Disney+ streaming service and highlighted the company's commitment to innovation and storytelling. Honorees shared their personal connections to Disney and expressed gratitude for the recognition.

title: Disney whistleblower told SEC the company inflated revenue for years
summary: A former Walt Disney Co. accountant has filed whistleblower tips with the SEC, alleging the company has materially overstated revenue for years. The individual, who was fired in 2017, claims Disney inflated its revenue figures. This news was initially published on August 19, 2019, and updated on August 24, 2019.

title: Target teams up with Disney on interactive in-store shops
summary: Target and Disney are collaborating to launch "store-within-a-store" concepts in 25 Target locations starting in October, with 40 more planned for the following year. This partnership aims to expand Disney's retail footprint beyond malls and offer an enhanced shopping experience with exclusive merchandise and interactive displays. Target CEO Brian Cornell highlighted Disney's unmatched appeal to families, while Disney executives noted the significant overlap between Disney fans and Target shoppers as a key driver for the collaboration.

title: Target, Disney partner on store displays to grab holiday sales
summary: Target and Disney are partnering on store displays to boost holiday sales. This collaboration aims to leverage both brands' appeal to attract shoppers during the critical holiday season.

title: Target to add 65 mini-Disney Stores, build new project near Animal Kingdom
summary: Target announced a new partnership with Disney, revealing plans to add 65 mini-Disney Stores within its existing toy departments and to build a new project near Animal Kingdom. This collaboration was unveiled at the D23 Expo in California, linking the retail giant with the theme park titan.

title: Disney to launch 25 stores inside Target nationwide in October
summary: Walt Disney Co. and Target Corp. announced a collaboration to open 25 Disney stores inside select Target locations nationwide on Oct. 4, with plans for 40 additional sites by October 2020. These "shop-in-shop" locations will feature over 450 Disney items, including more than 100 products previously exclusive to Disney stores, and will be operated by Target. The announcement highlights both companies' strategies to enhance customer experiences and drive growth, with Target also planning a new store at the Walt Disney World Resort.

title: Disney Gets Second Chance With Orlando’s Star Wars Land
summary: Walt Disney Co. is opening its second Star Wars-themed land, Galaxy's Edge, in Orlando, Florida, on Thursday. This opening differentiates from the first one in Anaheim, California, by eliminating many of the attendance restrictions that negatively impacted turnout. The Orlando park aims to avoid the lighter-than-expected crowds experienced in Anaheim.

title: Disney lays off nearly 60 employees in media distribution following Fox purchase
summary: Walt Disney Co. has laid off nearly 60 employees in its media distribution units, including home entertainment and TV distribution, following its acquisition of 21st Century Fox. These layoffs are part of an ongoing cost-cutting effort aiming for $2 billion in synergies by 2021, with expectations for up to 4,000 total job cuts from the merger. The redundancies also follow disappointing earnings reported by Disney, partly attributed to underperforming newly acquired Fox units.

title: WarnerMedia CEO John Stankey is promoted to AT&T president and chief operating officer
summary: John Stankey, the CEO of WarnerMedia, has been promoted to president and chief operating officer of AT&T Inc. He will continue to lead WarnerMedia and will report to AT&T Chairman and CEO Randall Stephenson. This move positions Stankey as a clear successor to Stephenson and comes as WarnerMedia and AT&T prepare to launch the HBO Max subscription service.

title: Toymaker Jakks Pacific gets a takeover offer from Jazwares’ parent
summary: Jakks Pacific Inc., a toymaker considering a sale, has received a takeover offer from Alleghany Corp., the parent company of rival Jazwares Inc. Alleghany offered to buy Jakks Pacific for 85 cents a share, valuing the company at approximately $27.7 million. This comes as toymakers consolidate to gain scale and diversify in the wake of Toys R Us's bankruptcy.

title: Disney Inks Long-Term Deal to Occupy Most of Pinewood Studios
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has secured a long-term deal to use most of Pinewood Studios outside London, including its stages and backlots, starting in 2020. This arrangement follows a similar deal between Netflix and Shepperton Studios, both owned by Pinewood Group, intensifying concerns about studio space scarcity in the UK for smaller production companies. Despite the growing demand in Britain, Pinewood Group is withdrawing from studio partnerships in Atlanta and Malaysia.

title: Target's loyalty program is expanding nationwide in October with perks for all shoppers
summary: Target is expanding its free loyalty program, Target Circle, nationwide in October, offering personalized deals and opportunities to support local non-profits. Shoppers will earn 1% on purchases to redeem later, receive a birthday discount, and can vote to direct Target's charitable giving. Existing RedCard holders will continue to receive 5% off purchases and can utilize other Target Circle perks, while the Cartwheel savings tool will be integrated and rebranded as "Target Circle offers."

title: Apple Says Apple TV+ Is Coming Nov. 1. Here’s How Much It Will Cost
summary: Apple announced that its video streaming service, Apple TV+, will launch on November 1 in over 100 countries for $4.99 monthly. Customers who purchase a new Apple device will receive one free year of Apple TV+. This announcement led to a nearly 3% dip in Netflix's stock and positions Apple TV+ to debut before Disney+'s launch.

title: Acquisitions: A look at Disney’s golden assets
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has made several highly successful acquisitions, including Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, and 21st Century Fox, which have significantly bolstered its content library and streaming capabilities. These strategic purchases, particularly the 21st Century Fox deal and its subsequent majority stake in Hulu, have contributed to consistent double-digit profit growth for Disney, with share gains of 23% in the past 12 months and 26% year-to-date.

title: Disney CEO Bob Iger resigns from Apple’s board of directors
summary: Disney CEO Bob Iger has resigned from Apple's board of directors, according to an SEC filing. The resignation comes as both Disney and Apple are preparing to launch their respective video streaming services, Disney+ and Apple TV+, in November, suggesting a potential conflict of interest due to competitive overlap. Iger had been a member of Apple's board since November 2011.

title: Netflix vs Apple: Here's which stock would have made you richer if you invested $1,000 10 years ago
summary: This article compares the returns of a $1,000 investment made 10 years ago in Netflix versus Apple. Netflix significantly outperformed Apple, turning $1,000 into nearly $47,400 compared to Apple's $10,400. The article also discusses Apple TV+'s launch and its potential impact on Netflix, noting that while Netflix's past returns are impressive, its future growth depends on subscriber retention amidst new competition.

title: Walt Disney Co. CEO Bob Iger leaves Apple’s board
summary: Walt Disney Co. CEO Bob Iger has departed Apple's board of directors as both companies prepare to launch competing video streaming services. Iger's departure on September 10th signals increased competition between Disney and Apple in the video streaming market. The move comes as Apple TV+ and Disney+ are set to launch later this year at competitive price points.

title: Netflix acquires the global streaming rights to ‘Seinfeld’
summary: Netflix has acquired the global streaming rights to all 180 episodes of "Seinfeld" in a five-year deal with Sony Pictures Television, set to begin in 2021. This move comes after Netflix lost streaming rights for "The Office" and "Friends" to rival services, and the deal is reportedly worth significantly more than the amounts paid for those shows. Hulu currently holds the domestic rights to "Seinfeld," which expire in 2021.

title: LATAM Airlines Group Reveals Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge-Inspired Stormtrooper Plane
summary: LATAM Airlines Group has unveiled a Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge-inspired Stormtrooper Plane, a Boeing 777 designed in conjunction with Disney and Lucasfilm. This themed aircraft, capable of seating 410 passengers, began commercial flights in October 2019, serving routes including Orlando, Miami, Madrid, Frankfurt, Paris, and London from its São Paulo/Guarulhos hub. The initiative is a promotional partnership with Disney, aiming to bring the excitement of Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge to passengers.

title: Walt Disney Co. Bob Iger’s Memoir On Apple: “If Steve (Jobs) Were Still Alive, We’d Have Combined Our Companies”
summary: In his new memoir, former Walt Disney Co. CEO Bob Iger reveals that he believes a merger between Disney and Apple would have occurred if Steve Jobs were still alive. Iger detailed his close relationship with Jobs and the previous animosity between the two companies before his tenure. This revelation comes as Disney and Apple are now streaming media rivals, with Iger recently resigning from Apple's board.

title: Microsoft customers gain a financial services advocate in new CVP Bill Borden
summary: Microsoft has appointed Bill Borden as Corporate Vice President of Financial Services, leveraging his 20 years of industry experience from Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Citigroup. Borden will lead Microsoft's go-to-market strategy in financial services, focusing on digital transformation and empowering intelligent banking solutions. His appointment underscores Microsoft's investment in industry-specific expertise to better serve its customers.

title: Netflix Stock Drops After CEO Acknowledges ‘Tough Competition’ Coming From Disney, Apple
summary: Netflix's stock dropped significantly after CEO Reed Hastings acknowledged the upcoming "tough competition" from Disney Plus and Apple TV Plus. Investors were unnerved by his comments, despite Netflix having previously addressed the increased competitive intensity in the streaming sector. An analyst, however, predicted a rebound for Netflix's stock, arguing that new entrants won't necessarily steal existing subscribers.

title: Walt Disney Co. Chairman/CEO Bob Iger Opens Up In Revealing New York Times Interview
summary: Walt Disney Co. Chairman/CEO Bob Iger gave an extensive interview to the New York Times, discussing his career trajectory, regrets, and key business decisions like the Lucasfilms and Fox deals. He also reflected on his humble beginnings, the challenges of executive leadership, and his reasons for passing on a Twitter acquisition due to brand concerns and societal impact. The interview precedes the release of his memoir, "The Ride of A Lifetime."

title: Netflix Stock Breaks Down as Competition Heats Up
summary: Netflix stock fell following increased competition from Apple and Disney, causing CEO Reed Hastings to emphasize the company's core strategy of in-house content. Despite concerns about subscriber misses, an analyst suggests that the broader trend of shifting to streaming will outweigh competitive headwinds. Technically, the stock is showing bearish indicators and could see further decline, with its next earnings report due on October 15, 2019.

title: Catherine Powell, President of Disney Parks Western Region, Leaving Walt Disney Company
summary: Catherine Powell, President of Disney Parks Western Region, is reportedly leaving the Walt Disney Company. Her position has been eliminated, and the heads of Walt Disney World, Disneyland, and Disneyland Paris will now report directly to Bob Chapek. Powell had been with the company for 15 years and oversaw significant projects, including the opening of Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.

title: HGTV HOME® by Sherwin-Williams Announces Its 2020 Color Collection of the Year
summary: HGTV HOME® by Sherwin-Williams has announced Romance as its 2020 Color of the Year, a soft blush hue evoking serenity. This color is part of the Simply Blissful 2020 Color Collection, which includes 10 complementary colors designed to help consumers create a glamorous and tranquil home space. The collection, available exclusively at Lowe's, aims to coordinate easily with existing décor, reflecting a desire for balance and self-care at home.

title: Netflix stock turns negative for 2019, but trader sees another big drop ahead
summary: Netflix stock has turned negative for 2019, with one trader predicting a further significant drop due to a lack of support on the charts until $231. This decline is attributed to increasing streaming competition and a recent decrease in subscriber numbers, leading analysts to advise investors to stay away from the stock for the near future.

title: Disney CEO Bob Iger Has Lessons On Fostering Creativity — And Acquiring It
summary: Bob Iger reflects on his 15 years as CEO of The Walt Disney Company in his new memoir, "The Ride of a Lifetime," discussing how he revitalized the company through strategic acquisitions like Pixar, Lucasfilm, and 21st Century Fox. He emphasizes the importance of risk-taking, processing failure in creative endeavors, and preserving the unique culture of acquired companies. Iger also shares insights into leadership, including the need for optimism and internal support, and how his personal background influenced his ambition.

title: The Walt Disney Company and PlayStation Vue Announce Comprehensive Distribution Agreement
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced a comprehensive multi-year distribution agreement with PlayStation Vue to continue providing its extensive lineup of sports, news, and entertainment content. This expanded deal includes newly acquired FX and National Geographic networks, as well as the ACC Network, reinforcing both companies' commitment to delivering premium video content across multiple platforms. PlayStation Vue subscribers will retain access to a wide array of Disney and ESPN channels, enhancing their personalized television viewing experience.

title: New Disney stores at Target now open, featuring 'Frozen 2' and Star Wars merchandise
summary: Target and Disney have launched 25 new "shop-in-shop" Disney stores within Target locations across the U.S., coinciding with the release of new merchandise for "Frozen 2" and "Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker." These 750-square-foot stores offer over 450 items, including many previously exclusive to Disney retail locations, and are designed to provide an immersive family shopping experience. The partnership plans to expand with another 40 locations by October 2020 and a new Target store near Walt Disney World Resort in 2021.

title: Naver, Kakao scramble to secure web cartoons
