summary: Naver and Kakao are heavily investing in securing intellectual property rights for web novels and cartoons to capitalize on the rapidly growing cultural content market. They are developing these original sources into diverse forms of cultural content like movies and TV shows, with both companies actively holding contests to attract new talent and expand their content libraries. The market for web novels and cartoons in Korea has seen explosive growth, driven by an increasing willingness of users to pay for quality content and the rise of smart devices.

title: Target Circle guide: Here's what you need to know about the new shopper loyalty program
summary: Target has expanded its free shopper loyalty program, Target Circle, nationwide. This program allows shoppers to earn 1% on purchases, receive personalized offers like a birthday discount, and help direct Target's charitable giving. While RedCard holders still get 5% off, they can also benefit from other Circle perks, as the new program integrates the former Cartwheel savings tool.

title: Shepard Smith Boosted Fox News’ Credibility, Not Its Bottom Line
summary: Shepard Smith's unexpected departure from Fox News is analyzed in terms of its impact on the network's credibility versus its financial bottom line. While Smith was seen as a journalistic asset, especially by mainstream media, his show was the lowest-rated on the Fox News schedule, and the network's financial engine relies more on its loyalist base and affiliate fees than individual show ratings or advertising from non-aligned sponsors. The article suggests that Fox News may find a more cost-effective host for his slot who is also more aligned with the network's core audience.

title: Omnicom and Publicis emerge as big winners in global Disney review
summary: Omnicom and Publicis have been named the big winners in the global Disney agency review. Both advertising agencies will be servicing The Walt Disney Co. through bespoke units. This decision comes after a comprehensive review process by Disney.

title: Target will offer free shipping, Disney shops this holiday season
summary: Target announced its holiday shopping plans, including free shipping with no minimum purchase and the expansion of Disney shops within its stores. The retailer is preparing for a shorter holiday season with various deals, exclusive toys, and perks for its new loyalty program members, competing with other retailers like Walmart and Best Buy. Target aims to strengthen its position in the toy market following the closure of Toys R Us.

title: Fly the Friendly Galaxy: United Airlines Joins Forces with Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker to Offer Customers Unforgettable Star Wars Experiences
summary: United Airlines has partnered with Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker to offer customers and employees unique Star Wars-themed experiences. This collaboration includes a special aircraft paint design, a new inflight safety video featuring Star Wars characters, and opportunities for MileagePlus members to bid on exclusive experiences like premiere access and travel packages to filming locations. The initiative aims to connect people and unite the world while promoting the final chapter of the Skywalker saga.

title: France’s Banijay Group enters into a deal to buy Endemol Shine Group
summary: France’s Banijay Group has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of the equity of Endemol Shine Group (ESG), co-owned by The Walt Disney Company and Apollo Global Management, Inc. The acquisition will create a content production and distribution powerhouse with almost 200 production companies in 23 territories and rights for close to 100,000 hours of content. While financial details were not disclosed, sources suggest the deal is valued around $2.2 billion and is expected to boost Banijay's industry position and intellectual property portfolio.

title: Banijay take the Endemol Shine Group
summary: Banijay has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Endemol Shine Group, a deal that will make Banijay owner of nearly 200 producers and rights to about 100,000 hours of content, with pro-form revenues expected to reach 3 billion euros. The acquisition, pending closure conditions, will include Endemol Shine's 120 production brands and over 4,300 registered formats, significantly broadening Banijay's intellectual property portfolio. The combined group will be led by LDH and Vivendi, with financing through a capital extension and debt financing involving Deutsche Bank, Natixis, and Société Générale.

title: Review: Bob Iger’s The Ride of A Lifetime: Lessons Learned From 15 Years as CEO of the Walt Disney Co.
summary: This review discusses Bob Iger's book, "The Ride of a Lifetime," highlighting its blend of personal and professional insights from his 15 years as CEO of The Walt Disney Company. The book delves into Iger's handling of major deals, including the acquisitions of Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, and FOX, and his interactions with prominent figures like Steve Jobs and George Lucas. While praising the book's insights into Disney's growth, the review also notes omissions regarding certain controversies and personnel issues during Iger's tenure.

title: AT&T offers free HBO Max to trump Verizon, Sprint in mobile 'Game of Thrones'
summary: AT&T is offering free HBO Max to mobile customers with a premium unlimited data plan to compete with rivals Verizon and Sprint. This move leverages content acquired from Time Warner and aims to counter similar streaming initiatives from other carriers. The service will include HBO and HBO Max content, launching in May 2020.

title: Banijay Group to Acquire Endemol Shine Group
summary: Banijay Group has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of the equity of Endemol Shine Group, co-owned by The Walt Disney Company and Apollo Global Management, Inc. This acquisition will position Banijay Group as a leader in content production and distribution, boasting nearly 200 production companies across 23 territories and rights to almost 100,000 hours of content. The combined entity is expected to generate approximately €3 billion in pro-forma revenue for 2019 and will include renowned brands like Black Mirror, Peaky Blinders, and MasterChef.

title: Walt Disney Company’s Investor Call Disney+ Highlights
summary: The Walt Disney Company's recent investor call highlighted details about Disney+, including its launch on Amazon, Samsung, and LG devices, and its European rollout on March 31st. Despite increased direct-to-consumer revenues, the segment operating loss grew due to Hulu consolidation and Disney+ launch costs. CEO Robert Iger also provided updates on the successful Disney+ trial in the Netherlands and mentioned FX content moving exclusively to Hulu.

title: Discovery looks to create its own Hulu by taking channels online
summary: Discovery Inc. is exploring the creation of its own streaming service, similar to Hulu, by combining its various TV channels for direct-to-consumer access in the U.S. This strategic shift aims to reach non-cable subscribers and combat cord-cutting, leveraging Discovery's unscripted programming, which is less costly to produce. The company plans to invest $300 million to $400 million in digital efforts in 2019 and is also developing specialized streaming services for sports, natural history, and home improvement content.

title: The Walt Disney Company Reports 4th Quarter and Full Year Earnings for Fiscal 2019
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported its Q4 and full fiscal year 2019 earnings, with Parks, Experiences and Products revenues increasing 8% to $6.7 billion and segment operating income up 17% to $1.4 billion. Growth was driven by merchandise licensing (especially Frozen and Toy Story), Disneyland Resort due to higher guest spending, and Disney Vacation Club sales. The report also notes the impact of Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge openings and anticipates further impact from upcoming Star Wars releases.

title: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph says company’s ‘secret weapon’ sets itself apart from Disney, other streaming services
summary: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph believes the company's "focus" on streaming and movies is its "secret weapon" against new competitors like Disney+ and Apple TV+. Despite growing competition and concerns about Netflix's revenue stream, Randolph emphasizes the company's startup mentality and willingness to adapt, assuring its continued presence in the evolving digital streaming landscape.

title: Gary Ehrlich Named President, General Manager of Fox Studio Lot
summary: Gary Ehrlich has been appointed President, General Manager of the Fox Studio Lot. This move is significant as Fox Corporation seeks to leverage its real estate assets after selling most of its entertainment assets to Disney. Ehrlich, with his background at Fox Sports and Live Nation, will oversee all operations and development of the valuable studio property.

title: Opinion | Nostalgia is the most powerful force in American culture right now. No one can sell you more of it than Disney.
summary: This opinion piece argues that nostalgia is the dominant cultural force in America, and Disney is uniquely positioned to capitalize on it, particularly through its new Disney Plus streaming service. The author suggests that while Disney Plus feeds nostalgia, it could have a negative impact on creativity within the entertainment industry. The article highlights the entry of Disney into the "streaming wars" and its potential influence.

title: MasterClass Announces Walt Disney Company Chairman and CEO Bob Iger to Teach Business Strategy & Leadership
summary: MasterClass announced that The Walt Disney Company Chairman and CEO, Bob Iger, will teach a class on business strategy and leadership, focusing on bold moves, smart risks, and embracing change, along with case studies of Disney's major acquisitions. The class will cover his strategies behind acquisitions like Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, and 21st Century Fox, as well as the launches of ESPN+ and Disney+. This offering aims to provide practical lessons and bold business strategies for professionals and leaders at all levels.

title: Where Is The Headquarters Of The Walt Disney Company?
summary: The Walt Disney Company's corporate headquarters is in Burbank, California, where it has been located since 1940. The article details the company's five principal business segments and its historical evolution from the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio founded in 1923. It also provides financial data for 2017 and 2018, showing a revenue increase to $59.4 billion in 2018.

title: “It was all started by a mouse” – But how big is The Walt Disney Company?
summary: This article explores the vast size and financial power of The Walt Disney Company, starting from its humble beginnings with Mickey Mouse. It highlights Disney's extensive corporate umbrella, including well-known subsidiaries like ESPN, ABC, Pixar, and Lucasfilm, as well as surprising ones like GoPro and A&E Networks. The piece also notes Disney's significant financial might, with its stock price breaking $150/share and a market cap of $262 Billion mentioned after the launch of Disney+.

title: Movie studios could buy theaters as U.S. seeks to end old limits
summary: The U.S. Justice Department is moving to terminate a 70-year-old antitrust settlement that prevented Hollywood studios from owning movie theaters and dictating which films they would show. This move, stemming from the 1948 Paramount Pictures consent decrees, is aimed at fostering "consumer-friendly innovation" as new entertainment services like Netflix have made the old rules irrelevant. While cinema chains' stocks rose on the news, some analysts are skeptical about major studios buying theater chains given the shift towards streaming.

title: Robservations: Entercom sets sights on new Chicago boss
summary: This article reports on several media industry updates in Chicago. Rachel Williamson is expected to succeed Jimmy de Castro as senior vice president and market manager of Entercom Chicago. Alex Salvi, a Chicago native, has launched a new nightly show on One America News Network. Angela Ingram of iHeartMedia Chicago was honored for her commitment to empowering women, and the article also notes the passing of Joe Aaron, founder of the Chicago Jewish News, and the birth of a child to Leah Hope and Bryan Smith.

title: FuboTV review: Great for streaming sports, but missing one big player
summary: This article provides a comprehensive review of fuboTV, a streaming service highly geared towards sports enthusiasts. While it offers a wide array of channels and strong sports coverage, it notably lacks ESPN and other Disney-owned channels, which is a significant drawback for some NFL and NBA fans. The review details fuboTV's packages, pricing, user interface, and compares it to competitors like Sling TV and Hulu + Live TV.

title: For ‘Frozen 2,’ Toy Makers Let It Flow
summary: Toy makers like Hasbro Inc. and Jakks Pacific Inc. are heavily producing merchandise for "Frozen 2," including dolls and play sets, to avoid the product shortages that occurred with the original "Frozen" film in 2013. Walt Disney Co. and its licensing partners have expanded the merchandise offerings for the sequel, learning from past experiences and leveraging the established popularity of the characters. This strategy aims to capitalize on the film's release and meet consumer demand more effectively.

title: ‘Frozen 2’ can’t help sagging box office sales
summary: Despite the strong opening of Disney's "Frozen 2," box office sales are projected to dip by 4% this year, largely due to several movie flops and increased competition from streaming services. Analysts predict that even highly anticipated upcoming blockbusters won't save 2019 from being a weak year, with a flat performance at best, and 2020 also looking challenged before a potential "phenomenal year" in 2021. The industry is grappling with changing consumer habits, as more streaming options like Netflix and Disney+ become available.

title: Trump’s comments, Disney push Wall Street to new high
summary: Wall Street's main indexes reached new highs on Tuesday, driven by positive comments from President Donald Trump regarding trade negotiations with China and strong performances from Walt Disney Co (DIS.N) and Best Buy Co Inc (BBY.N). Despite some weak economic data, investor optimism was fueled by hopes for a trade truce, upbeat economic indicators, and interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. The consumer discretionary sector performed strongly thanks to Best Buy's holiday-quarter profit forecast, though Dollar Tree Inc (DLTR.O) saw a significant drop due to a weaker outlook.

title: For $90, Bob Iger Will Teach You How To Run The Walt Disney Company
summary: Masterclass.com is offering an online course taught by Bob Iger, chairman and CEO of The Walt Disney Company, for $90. The series of 13 pre-recorded video lessons covers Iger's leadership strategies, including negotiation, time management, and his M&A strategy that led to Disney's acquisition of Pixar, Marvel, and 21st Century Fox. This class provides insights into Iger's 14-year tenure, which shaped Disney's shift to streaming and major acquisitions.

title: Why ‘Frozen’ and ‘Star Wars’ matter so much to toy makers this holiday season
summary: Toy manufacturers like Hasbro and Mattel are heavily relying on licensed intellectual property from popular movies and other digital content, such as "Frozen 2" and "Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker," to drive sales during the holiday season. The article highlights the growing trend of licensing in the toy industry, extending beyond films and TV to video games, streaming, and YouTube, as well as toy makers licensing their own brands to entertainment platforms. Despite flat overall U.S. toy sales, the industry remains resilient, with strong demand for traditional toys amidst parental concerns about excessive screen time.

title: Frenan fusión Disney-Fox en México: Televisa obtuvo una orden judicial
summary: A judge in Mexico has granted Grupo Televisa SAB an injunction, delaying Walt Disney Co.'s USD 71 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox Inc.'s entertainment assets in the country. Televisa argued that the Federal Telecommunications Institute (IFT) unfairly dismissed their concerns about competition threats posed by the merger. The judge ordered the IFT to conduct a new investigation into the matter, potentially causing few repercussions for Disney outside of Mexico as the financial transaction had already closed.

title: Cisco Unveils Plan for Building Internet for the Next Decade of Digital Innovation
summary: Cisco has announced its 'Internet for the Future' strategy, based on significant investments in Silicon+Optics+Software. This initiative introduces Cisco Silicon One, a unified silicon architecture for the network, and the new Cisco 8000 Series routers. The strategy aims to reduce costs and enhance capabilities for mass-scale networks to support future digital innovations like 5G, AI, and 16K streaming.

title: Hasbro Announces The Child (AKA ‘Baby Yoda’) Toys From The Mandalorian
summary: Hasbro has announced a new line of Star Wars products featuring "The Child" (AKA 'Baby Yoda') from Disney+'s The Mandalorian, available for preorder and shipping in May 2020. The collection includes various figures and a talking plush toy, with additional products to be revealed later. These toys aim to capitalize on the popular character's widespread fan reaction.

title: Sustainable Leadership: What Drove Tracy Liu Toward WAYB
summary: This article features an interview with Tracy Liu, COO of WAYB, a baby-gear startup focused on sustainable products. She discusses her journey from the Walt Disney Company to WAYB, driven by a desire to build a mission-driven, family-focused company. Liu also shares insights on being a woman in the C-suite, the value of sustainability for the next generation of business leaders, and advice for women entering the sustainability field.

title: Michael Jackson Estate, Walt Disney Co. Settle Copyright Dispute Over Music, Images Of The Late Singer
summary: The Michael Jackson estate and The Walt Disney Company have settled a copyright lawsuit stemming from the ABC-TV special "The Last Days Of Michael Jackson." The dispute involved the unauthorized use of Jackson's image and music in the 2018 special. The settlement was confirmed by the Jackson estate's lawyer, Howard Weitzman.

title: Netflix was the best-performing stock of the decade, delivering a more than 4,000% return
summary: Netflix emerged as the top-performing stock of the decade, achieving an astounding return of over 4,000% for investors who bought in early. Despite perennial skepticism from analysts regarding its financial metrics and increasing competition, the company's strategic expansion into international markets and significant investment in original content have been key drivers of its success. Netflix also leverages its platform to offer creative autonomy to filmmakers, attracting top talent and high-quality productions.

title: You'll Soon Be Able to Bring Home Your Own Baby Yoda at Build-a-Bear Workshop
summary: Build-a-Bear Workshop announced that a plush toy version of "The Child" from Disney+'s The Mandalorian, affectionately known as Baby Yoda, will be available for purchase in the coming months. CEO Sharon Price John revealed this news, highlighting Baby Yoda's significant online popularity. This move follows other companies capitalizing on the character's widespread appeal since its debut.

title: Can Baby Yoda save Build-A-Bear?
summary: Build-A-Bear, once a successful toy company that went public in 2004, has seen its financial fortunes decline significantly due to struggles in brick-and-mortar retail. The company's stock, which once hit $36.90, averaged $4.37 over the last year, leading to predictions of zero growth or a small drop for the fiscal year 2019. However, the announcement of a Baby Yoda plush toy, a collaboration with Disney's popular "The Mandalorian" series, caused Build-A-Bear's stock to skyrocket 15%, offering a potential lifeline for the struggling retailer.

title: ‘Fortune’ Names Disney Among the “World’s Most Admired Companies” for 2020
summary: The Walt Disney Company has been recognized by Fortune as one of the "World's Most Admired Companies" for 2020, ranking No. 4 overall for the second consecutive year. Disney also secured the top spot in the entertainment industry for the 17th year in a row and received the highest marks across all industries for its "quality of products and services." The recognition highlights Disney's high performance in areas such as people management, quality of management, long-term investment value, social responsibility, and global competitiveness.

title: Disney Experiences: Magic through Imagination & Innovation
summary: Disney Experiences focuses on bringing Disney stories to life globally through theme parks, resorts, cruise ships, and products. The article highlights how the company leverages imagination and innovation to create magical experiences, detailing its diverse portfolio and significant economic impact. It also covers recent news and upcoming initiatives like "Soarin' Across America" and the collaboration with Formula 1.

title: Hasbro Soars After Profit Tops Estimates on Frozen 2 Toys
summary: Hasbro Inc. reported earnings that exceeded analysts' estimates, driven by strong sales of toys from "Frozen 2" and "Star Wars," despite challenges from the trade war with China. The company's profit per share, excluding some items, significantly surpassed projections, while revenue rose 3% to $1.43 billion. Shares saw their largest jump in nearly seven months following the announcement.

title: Box Office: IMAX Positions ‘I Still Believe’ As Next Big Faith-Based Hit
summary: Lionsgate's faith-based drama "I Still Believe" is set to become the first of its genre to play in IMAX, an unusual move highlighting its potential as a major mainstream hit. The film, from the Erwin Brothers, concerns musician Jeremy Camp and his relationship with his first wife, and will have an IMAX-exclusive sneak preview before its general release. This strategic IMAX positioning is seen as Lionsgate's declaration that "I Still Believe" will be the year's big faith-based theatrical success, following a trend of successful Christian films.

title: Hasbro Revenue Boosted by Frozen 2 and Star Wars Products
summary: Hasbro, Inc. reported increased revenues for Q4 and full-year 2019, driven by strong demand for products related to Disney's Frozen 2 and Star Wars. Despite a decrease in some Franchise Brands like Nerf and My Little Pony, Partner Brands saw significant growth, notably from Marvel's Avengers and Spider-Man franchises. The company's executives highlighted the successful execution of channel strategy, growth in Magic: The Gathering, and the strategic acquisition of Entertainment One to expand its global play and entertainment presence.

title: Could Roku Stock Hit $450?
summary: This article analyzes how Roku's stock could reach $450 by 2025, a significant increase from its 2020 levels of around $130. The analysis outlines key factors required for this growth, including a substantial increase in active accounts to 125 million, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) to over $50, and improved net income margins to 22.5%. The Trefis team details the assumptions behind this optimistic forecast, contrasting it with a downside case for Roku stock.

title: Fox in Talks to Acquire Free-Streaming Service Tubi for Over $500 Million (Report)
summary: Fox Corp. is reportedly in discussions to acquire the ad-supported free streaming service Tubi for over $500 million. This acquisition would add a dedicated streaming component with over 20,000 older TV shows and movies to Fox's portfolio, aiming to capitalize on the surge in internet-video viewing. The potential deal highlights the increasing activity in the ad-supported streaming market, following similar acquisitions and planned launches by competitors.

title: Build-A-Bear unveils Baby Yoda toy coming to stores this spring
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop announced the upcoming release of a Baby Yoda plush toy, generating excitement among fans of "The Mandalorian." While an exact release date in spring has not been specified, fans can sign up for email updates. This release follows other companies like Mattel and Funko also offering "The Child" merchandise, with Disney and Lucasfilm intentionally delaying merchandise to preserve the character's surprise debut.

title: Comcast Acquires Xumo Free-Streaming Video Service
summary: Comcast announced its acquisition of Xumo, a free advertising-supported streaming service, from Panasonic and Meredith Corp. for over $100 million. Xumo will continue to operate as an independent business unit within Comcast Cable, maintaining its 190+ free channels and leveraging its 10 million monthly viewers to promote Comcast's forthcoming Peacock service. This acquisition is part of Comcast's larger strategy in the streaming space as it prepares for the hybrid subscription/free model launch of Peacock.

title: Meet the 10 most overpaid CEOs in the U.S.
summary: A report titled "The 100 Most Overpaid CEOs" identifies the top 10 most overpaid chief executives in the U.S., comparing their compensation to total shareholder return and median employee salaries. The report highlights extreme pay disparities and suggests that increased shareholder pressure and policy changes might lead to more performance-linked compensation. Historically, CEO-to-worker pay ratios were significantly lower, and current movements aim to address this widening gap through legislation and tax reforms.

title: Bob Chapek Named Chief Executive Officer of The Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that Bob Chapek has been named Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. Robert A. Iger will assume the role of Executive Chairman through 2021, focusing on creative endeavors and ensuring a smooth transition. The Board cited Chapek's 27 years of leadership experience and successful track record across Disney's Parks, Consumer Products, and Studio businesses.

title: Bob Iger Steps Down As Walt Disney Company CEO, Replaced By Bob Chapek
summary: Robert A. Iger has stepped down as CEO of The Walt Disney Company, nearly two years before his contract was due to expire, and Bob Chapek, former chairman of Disney Parks, experiences and products, has been named his successor. Iger will transition to executive chairman until December 31, 2021, focusing on creative endeavors. The surprise announcement has generated mixed reactions from former executives, market analysts, and Disney fans, particularly those concerned about Chapek's impact on theme park experiences and budget management.

title: These are the 10 most ‘overpaid’ CEOs in the S&P 500, according to a new study
summary: A new study identified the 10 most "overpaid" CEOs in the S&P 500 Index, based on factors like CEO pay, stock performance, shareholder votes against pay deals, and pay comparison to the average worker. The report also criticized major fund companies, including those managing popular S&P 500 ETFs, for not adequately addressing executive compensation. Notably, Disney's Bob Iger was included in this list shortly after moving to an executive chairman role.

title: New JPMorgan Chase CMO has come a long way from telesales gig
summary: Leslie Gillin has been appointed as the new Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) at JPMorgan Chase, capping a 30-year career that began in telemarketing at MBNA America. In her new role, Gillin oversees marketing for the Chase, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and J.P. Morgan brands, emphasizing customer-centric strategies, data leverage, and strategic partnerships. She plans to focus on aligning marketing goals with business objectives, enhancing ROI on marketing spend, and optimizing omnichannel targeting.

title: Jakks Pacific at Toy Fair 2020: Kitty Catfe, Disney, and more
summary: Jakks Pacific unveiled several new toys at Toy Fair 2020, featuring popular franchises like Disney, Kitty Catfe, and Sonic. Highlights included large-scale Playdate Elsa and Water Nokk figures with interactive features, new Kitty Catfe collectibles in Boba cups, and a transforming Optimus Prime costume. The company also showcased new lines for Last Kids on Earth and Gigantosaurus, and an updated Creepy Crawler maker.

title: Bob Iger says Disney is ‘sobered’ by coronavirus outbreak
summary: During Walt Disney Co.'s annual shareholder meeting, Executive Chairman Bob Iger addressed concerns about the growing coronavirus outbreak, acknowledging its impact on the company's global operations, including the closure of theme parks. He highlighted Disney's resilience in past crises and officially introduced Bob Chapek as the new CEO. The meeting also covered the financial impacts of the virus, upcoming movie releases, Disney+ subscriber numbers, and shareholder votes on executive compensation and lobbying disclosure.

title: Byron Allen Makes $8.5B Cash Bid For Broadcaster Tegna
summary: Media entrepreneur Byron Allen has made an all-cash bid of $8.5 billion for broadcaster Tegna, offering $20 a share. This bid competes with offers from Gray Television and Apollo Global Management, both also at $20 a share, with Gray's being a cash and stock combination. One of Tegna's largest shareholders, Standard General, has urged the company to thoroughly evaluate all acquisition proposals to maximize shareholder value.

title: Disneyland, Disney World, Universal Studios Hollywood to Close Due to Coronavirus
summary: Disneyland, Walt Disney World, and Universal Studios Hollywood are closing their parks due to the coronavirus outbreak. This marks only the fourth time Disneyland has closed since 1955. Numerous other entertainment venues, including SeaWorld, Paramount Studio Tours, Sony Pictures Studio Tour, and Warner Bros. tours, are also suspending operations.

title: Coronavirus reverses Disney’s fortunes, for now
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted The Walt Disney Co., causing its stock to fall nearly 30% and leading to the closure of theme parks, suspension of film productions, and disruption of live sports programming for ESPN. While analysts expect a short-term financial hit, they anticipate Disney's strong intellectual property and diversified operations will allow it to recover within a few years. The turmoil also casts a new light on Bob Iger's recent decision to step down as CEO.

title: Norwegian, Royal Caribbean join Disney, Princess, other cruise lines halting operations
summary: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings and Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. announced the temporary suspension of their cruise operations due to the coronavirus outbreak, following similar decisions by Disney Cruise Line and Princess Cruises. This move, which impacts multiple brands and ships, aims to prioritize public health and safety, with most suspensions lasting approximately 30 days. Cruise lines are offering refunds or future cruise credits to affected passengers.

title: Coronavirus: Largest U.S. restaurant firm outlines emergency pay for workers & more
summary: Darden Restaurants, the parent company of Olive Garden, announced emergency pay for its employees to ensure restaurants can continue operating during the coronavirus pandemic. The company is actively in discussions with Washington D.C. leaders to explore using government relief funds to support employee compensation during this period.

title: Disney, reeling from the coronavirus, raises $6 billion in debt offering
summary: The Walt Disney Co. raised nearly $6 billion in a debt offering to shore up its debt structure amid the coronavirus outbreak and its economic impact. The company plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including restructuring debt and investments, while acknowledging significant business disruptions due to the pandemic. The offering comes after Disney's parks closed, cruises suspended, and movie releases delayed, further exacerbating its debt load from the $71-billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox.

title: U.S. TV Viewing Is Increasing During Coronavirus Pandemic
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, U.S. TV viewing significantly increased, with cable news networks seeing a 73% rise and financial news networks experiencing an even larger bump. Both broadcast networks and children's programming also showed notable increases, particularly in daytime and early fringe hours, as millions of Americans stayed home and turned to television for news and entertainment. Comscore continues to monitor these shifting consumption trends across its extensive footprint.

title: Coronavirus news: Disneyland, Walt Disney World to remain closed 'until further notice' amid COVID-19 outbreak
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that Disneyland Resort and Walt Disney World will remain closed "until further notice" due to the novel coronavirus outbreak, extending their temporary closures previously set through March. The company stated that the safety of guests and employees is its top priority and decided to continue paying hourly parks and resorts cast members through April 18. This decision reflects the ongoing uncertainty and complexity of the COVID-19 pandemic, aligning with expert and governmental guidance.

title: Disney’s Bob Iger to forgo salary amid coronavirus crisis
summary: Walt Disney Co. Executive Chairman Bob Iger will forgo his salary starting in April due to the financial impact of the coronavirus crisis, which has closed theme parks and halted film productions. Other senior executives, including CEO Bob Chapek, will also take salary reductions to help shoulder the burden of the pandemic's effects on the company. This decision comes as Disney faces widespread disruptions, including park closures, halted cruise lines, closed retail stores, and delayed film releases like "Mulan" and "Black Widow."

title: BREAKING: Walt Disney Company Senior Executives Take Salary Cuts Due to Unprecedented Disney Parks COVID-19 Closures
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced significant salary cuts for its senior executives in response to the unprecedented financial impact of COVID-19 and the indefinite closure of Disney Parks worldwide. CEO Bob Chapek will have his salary reduced by 50%, while Bob Iger has agreed to forgo 100% of his salary, affecting VPs, SVPs, and EVPs as well. These temporary cuts will remain in effect until the company sees a substantive recovery in its business.

title: Comcast and Fox Corp. Set Broad New Carriage Agreement
summary: Comcast and Fox Corp. have reached a long-term carriage agreement covering all of Fox’s cable channels, including Fox News, and its owned-and-operated local TV stations. This deal is significant for Fox Corp. due to Comcast’s extensive distribution footprint and includes authenticated streaming rights with dynamic advertising. The agreement was finalized without disputes, a reflection of the current economic climate, and ensures Xfinity customers will continue to receive Fox's programming.

title: Film News Roundup: ViacomCBS Closes $375 Million Deal for 49% of Miramax
summary: ViacomCBS has finalized its $375 million acquisition of a 49% stake in Miramax from beIN Media Group, gaining access to Miramax's extensive library of nearly 800 titles. The deal also includes an exclusive distribution agreement for Miramax's film library with Paramount Pictures and a first-look agreement for new film and TV projects. Separately, Imax hired Brett Harriss as SVP of investor relations, and Magnolia Home Entertainment is releasing several documentaries On Demand early due to the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Disney Furloughs Hit Film Labels, Including Marvel and Lucasfilm
summary: The Walt Disney Company's previously announced furloughs have impacted its premium film labels, including Marvel, Lucasfilm, Pixar, and Searchlight. These furloughs primarily affect staffers whose job duties cannot be performed due to ongoing coronavirus-related shutdowns. This move follows a Disney stock downgrade and highlights the widespread impact of revenue loss from the company's parks business.

title: Walt Disney Co. Enters New $5 Billion Credit Agreement
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has entered into a new 364-day credit agreement with Citibank for up to $5 billion, following similar agreements earlier in March. This comes as the company's theme parks and resorts are shut down globally due to the coronavirus pandemic, impacting a significant portion of its revenue. Despite the challenges, Disney's streaming service, Disney Plus, has reached 50 million paid subscribers.

title: Walt Disney CEO Bob Chapek Takes A Seat On The Company’s Board
summary: Walt Disney's new CEO, Bob Chapek, has been elected to the company's board of directors, a move anticipated since he took the top job in late February. The decision comes as Chapek has demonstrated leadership during the unprecedented challenges posed by the coronavirus pandemic. Former CEO Robert Iger and independent Lead Director Susan Arnold expressed their satisfaction with Chapek joining the board.

title: Netflix Now Worth More Than The Walt Disney Company
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Netflix surpassed Disney in market capitalization as Disney's parks and film studios shut down, severely impacting its revenue. Netflix's stock hit an all-time high of $426.75 per share, giving it a market cap of $187.3 billion, slightly higher than Disney's $186.6 billion. Analysts expect Netflix to continue to grow its subscriber base significantly as more people stay home, while Disney faces an arduous process to reopen and reshape its park experience.

title: Bob Chapek Elected to The Walt Disney Company Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company has elected CEO Bob Chapek to its board of directors. This move was not unexpected, as his election to the board was part of his employment agreement when he was named CEO seven weeks prior. The board acknowledged his decisive leadership during recent unprecedented challenges.

title: Coronavirus pandemic and online media consumption: settling into the New Normal
summary: This article discusses how online media consumption in Europe has begun to level off after an initial surge during the early stages of the coronavirus pandemic lockdown. It highlights that the "new normal" has settled in, with some categories that saw initial growth, such as General News, Instant Messaging, Food/Groceries Retail, and Entertainment, now showing signs of fatigue as activity stabilizes. The piece also includes a timeline of key pandemic events in Europe leading up to the lockdowns.

title: Disney Holds Millions Of DraftKings Shares Following Public Listing
summary: The Walt Disney Company owns over 18.2 million shares of DraftKings stock, valued at more than $364 million, following DraftKings' recent public listing. Disney acquired this stake through its purchase of 21st Century Fox in March 2019 and is designated as a "passive investor," prohibiting active involvement in DraftKings' operations or investments in direct competitors. This clarifies Disney's near-term strategy for its DraftKings investment, which originated from Fox's earlier investment in the daily fantasy sports operator.

title: Disney Stock Downgrade Could Be The Beginning of Unmagical Times
summary: Walt Disney Co. shares experienced a decline after MoffettNathanson downgraded the stock to "neutral" and lowered its price target due to increased risk and uncertainty across Disney’s businesses. This downgrade comes ahead of the company's planned earnings report, emphasizing concerns about the long-term economic impact of the pandemic. While one analyst maintained an "overweight" rating, the sector faces significant challenges due to reduced tourism and consumer reluctance to travel.

title: Disney Takes $1.4 Billion Hit to Earnings as Coronavirus Takes Hold
summary: Walt Disney Co. announced a $1.4 billion hit to its earnings due to the coronavirus pandemic, with more financial impact expected. The theme-parks division was most affected, but the company anticipates the global economic fallout will impact all its business segments. This comes after a successful previous year marked by blockbusters, popular theme parks, and a new streaming service.

title: Disney raises $11 billion in debt amid coronavirus crisis, as Shanghai park returns
summary: Walt Disney Co. has raised nearly $11 billion in new debt to mitigate the financial impact of the coronavirus crisis, which has closed its theme parks and halted productions. The company stated the funds would be used for general corporate purposes, including debt repayment, as it faces an estimated $1 billion hit to operating income from park closures. This debt raise comes as Shanghai Disneyland reopens with strict capacity limits, offering a glimpse of potential recovery for Disney's global operations.

title: MGM Resorts International reveals safety plan for reopening, asks guests to wear masks on casino floor
summary: MGM Resorts International has announced a seven-point safety plan for reopening its properties, developed with medical and scientific experts to prevent the spread of COVID-19. The plan includes mandatory masks for employees, encouraged mask-wearing for guests, temperature checks, physical distancing, enhanced cleaning, and digital innovations. MGM did not provide a specific reopening date but indicated that Bellagio and New York, New York, would be among the first to reopen.

title: ‘Hamilton’ Film Coming Exclusively to Disney+ Beginning July 3
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that the filmed version of the Broadway musical "Hamilton" will premiere exclusively on Disney+ on July 3, 2020, significantly earlier than planned. Lin-Manuel Miranda, Jeffrey Seller, and Thomas Kail collaborated with Disney to bring this award-winning stage musical to the streaming service. The film features the original Broadway cast and offers an intimate cinematic experience of the show.

title: Disney’s Purchase of 21st Century FOX Explained
summary: This article explains Disney's acquisition of 21st Century Fox, detailing the motivations behind the deal, including the rise of Netflix and the streaming revolution. It outlines the assets Disney gained, such as 20th Century Fox studios, a controlling share of Hulu, and the rights to Marvel characters like X-Men, Deadpool, and Fantastic 4. The article also clarifies which assets were spun off into the Fox Corporation and discusses the broader implications of the merger for the evolving media landscape.

title: Josh D’Amaro Named Chairman of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products and Rebecca Campbell Named Chairman of Disney’s Direct-to-Consumer and International
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced key leadership changes, naming Josh D’Amaro as Chairman, Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, and Rebecca Campbell as Chairman, Direct-to-Consumer and International. Both executives will report to CEO Bob Chapek and bring over two decades of experience to their new roles. The announcement also included appointments for leadership roles across Walt Disney World Resort, Disneyland Resort, Consumer Products, Games and Publishing, and Disney Signature Experiences.

title: The Walt Disney Company - A Leader In Corporate Social Responsibility
summary: The Walt Disney Company is recognized as a leader in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), focusing on the environment, community, and labor standards. Disney's CSR efforts include extensive volunteerism, significant charitable contributions, and environmental education through its films and conservation funds, demonstrating commitment to responsible business practices globally.

title: 21st Century Fox completes asset divestment, creates Fox Corp
summary: 21st Century Fox has created Fox Corporation as a standalone company to divest assets in anticipation of its acquisition by The Walt Disney Company. Fox Corp will house Fox broadcasting network, Fox Sports, Fox News, and Fox Business Network, with Michael Nathanson projecting a significant portion of its earnings from Fox News. The new board members include Lachlan Murdoch, Paul Ryan, Chase Carey, Roland Hernandez, and Anne Dias.

title: NEWS: The Walt Disney Company Appoints New Treasurer
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced the appointment of Carlos Gómez as its new Treasurer, succeeding the retiring John Headley. Gómez, who has been with Disney for 22 years and served as VP of Investor Relations, will report to CFO Christine McCarthy and oversee global treasury operations. He played a key role in the acquisitions of 20th Century Fox, Marvel, and Pixar.

title: SeaWorld announces plans for Orlando park to reopen. Here's what to expect
summary: SeaWorld's Orlando park plans to reopen on June 11, nearly four months after closing due to the coronavirus pandemic, pending final approval from Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis. The park will implement several new safety measures including mandatory face coverings, social distancing guidelines, increased cleaning, temperature screenings for guests and employees, and modifications to animal exhibits and interactions. Interim CEO Marc Swanson expects demand to return, especially from visitors who can drive to the park.

title: AMD’s Lisa Su Takes The No. 1 Position As S&P 500’s Highest Paid CEO
summary: Dr. Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, has been identified as the highest-paid chief executive in the S&P 500 for 2019, with total compensation of $58.5 million, a 338% year-over-year growth. Her compensation was largely comprised of stock awards, reflecting AMD's significant stock market gains and market share growth under her leadership. The article details AMD's recent performance, including strong notebook sales and GPU market share increases, and touches upon upcoming product plans.

title: AMD Stock Pushes Lisa Su to Top of CEO Compensation List
summary: Lisa Su, CEO of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), topped the annual CEO compensation survey by the Associated Press in 2019 with a $58.5 million pay package, largely due to AMD's strong stock performance. She is the first woman to achieve this No. 1 ranking. Her leadership is credited with turning around AMD, focusing the company on high-growth areas like high-performance computing, computer graphics, and graphics processing units.

title: Six Flags could be blueprint for U.S. parks
summary: Six Flags Entertainment Corp. has released comprehensive safety protocols for reopening its U.S. theme parks, setting a potential standard for the industry. These measures include temperature checks, mandatory masks, social distancing, and limited attendance. Other major theme park companies like Disney and Universal are also developing their own reopening plans, with industry experts predicting similar safety protocols across the board.

title: Disney Pledges $5M For NAACP And Other Groups Advancing Social Justice
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has pledged $5 million to support nonprofit organizations advancing social justice, with an initial $2 million donation going to the NAACP. This initiative follows the death of George Floyd and aims to eliminate disparities and racial discrimination through advocacy and education programs. CEO Bob Chapek stated that the pledge is part of Disney's ongoing commitment to social justice causes.

title: National Grid Partners Announces New Investments in Two Security Leaders
summary: National Grid Partners announced new investments in two leading online security companies, 1touch.io and RiskIQ, to enhance data security and combat cyber threats. The investments, totaling $14 million and $15 million respectively, highlight National Grid's commitment to delivering a safer energy future. These security solutions are particularly relevant given the increased remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Comcast unveils $100-million social justice plan amid George Floyd protests
summary: Comcast Corp. announced a $100-million social justice plan, allocating $75 million in cash and $25 million in advertising inventory over three years, in response to nationwide protests against police brutality. This initiative follows similar pledges from other major media and entertainment companies and aims to support organizations fighting injustice and to promote diversity and inclusion. The plan includes accelerating diversity training, supporting Black voices, and addressing internet access disparities for low-income communities.

title: Disney Parks, Experiences and Products Proposes Plans for the Disneyland Resort to Begin a Phased Reopening July 9, with Proposed Reopening of the Theme Parks July 17
summary: Disney Parks, Experiences and Products has proposed a phased reopening for the Disneyland Resort, starting with Downtown Disney District on July 9, and the theme parks (Disneyland park and Disney California Adventure park) on July 17. The reopening plans are pending state and local government approvals and will include significantly limited capacity, a new reservation system for park entry, and enhanced health and safety measures. Hotel reopening for Disney’s Grand Californian Hotel & Spa and Disney’s Paradise Pier Hotel is planned for July 23, with certain experiences like parades and character meet and greets returning at a later date.

title: How did Disney buy Marvel?
summary: Disney acquired Marvel Entertainment in 2009 for $4 billion, a move that set the stage for its highly successful Marvel Cinematic Universe. Despite internal resistance from some executives concerned about Marvel's "edgy" image affecting Disney's wholesome brand, the acquisition allowed Disney to expand its catalog with thousands of characters and broaden its appeal to young audiences. The MCU films have achieved critical and commercial success, with "Avengers: Endgame" grossing nearly $2.8 billion globally.

title: Norwegian, Oceania, Regent cruise lines extend suspensions into fall
summary: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd., which operates Norwegian, Oceania, and Regent Seven Seas, has extended its sailing suspensions through September 30, with some cancellations into October, due to travel and port restrictions. This further delay comes after previous plans to resume sailings in August, with the CEO emphasizing a gradual and safe relaunch focused on enhanced health measures. Other major cruise lines, including Disney, Cunard, P&O Cruises, AIDA Cruises, MSC Cruises, Royal Caribbean, and Princess Cruises have also extended suspensions, with some extending into late 2020 and even 2021.

title: For Walt Disney Co., a Stricken Empire (Published 2020)
summary: The coronavirus pandemic has devastated Walt Disney Co., turning its vast empire, once a strength, into a liability. Its theme parks, movie studios, cruise lines, and theatrical productions are largely shut down, leading to furloughs, pay cuts, and a significant drop in anticipated profits. Despite challenges, Disney's streaming services, particularly Disney+, are surging in subscribers, and its cable networks like ESPN are seeing reduced costs, offering some resilience amidst the widespread impact.

title: Special Feature: YouTube’s Evolution in the OTT Streaming Landscape...
summary: This article by Comscore and YouTube examines YouTube's significant growth within the evolving OTT streaming landscape, highlighting its increased reach in ad-supported households and substantial growth in CTV watch time. It also details how YouTube's unique user-generated content and extensive library are providing new opportunities for advertisers to target diverse audiences. The piece further explores emerging content consumption trends on the platform, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: fuboTV follows YouTube's lead, increases monthly subscription rate
summary: FuboTV is raising its monthly subscription rate from $60 to $65 for its family plan, and existing standard plan subscribers will be automatically moved to the family plan, increasing their rates from $55 to $65. This price hike comes alongside significant content changes, as fuboTV has dropped all Turner channels but added Disney channels, including ESPN, which will be available in August. The move follows a similar price increase by YouTube TV and suggests a potential trend in the streaming service market.

title: An updated timeline of price hikes at YouTube TV and other vMVPDs
summary: This article provides an updated timeline of price increases implemented by major virtual MVPDs (vMVPDs) such as YouTube TV, AT&T TV Now, FuboTV, Hulu, PlayStation Vue, and Sling TV. It details specific date-by-date price hikes and the reasons provided by companies, often citing rising content costs and expanded channel lineups. The timeline covers a period from February 2018 to July 2020, highlighting trends and significant events like PlayStation Vue's shutdown.

title: VOD Transactions Peaked in the Month of April 2020
summary: Comscore reports that Video on Demand (VOD) transactions, including Transactional on Demand (TOD), Subscription Video on Demand (SVOD), and Free on Demand (FOD), all peaked in April 2020 during the initial months of the coronavirus pandemic. While TOD and FOD remained steady or saw slight declines in May, SVOD transactions showed a more pronounced decline. The report specifically highlights significant year-over-year increases in Sports and Fitness VOD categories, suggesting a strong consumer interest in these areas during lockdown.

title: Crowds flock to Six Flags Great Adventure ready to have some fun, masks in place
summary: Six Flags Great Adventure reopened its gates after a coronavirus pause, drawing large crowds despite new safety protocols. Guests were required to wear masks, have their temperatures checked, and practice social distancing, with rides operating at reduced capacity. The park, a major seasonal employer, implemented these measures after Governor Phil Murphy allowed amusement parks to open at 50% capacity.

title: Lucie Quenneville Appointed General Manager, Programming and Strategies Acquisition, Bell Media
summary: Bell Media has appointed Lucie Quenneville as General Manager, Programming and Strategies Acquisition for its French-language content in Québec, effective July 20. Quenneville will oversee programming and acquisition strategies for V, Bell Media's French-language specialty channels, and Crave's French-language content. She brings 25 years of experience, including her recent role at CBC/Radio-Canada, and her appointment aims to strengthen Bell Media's French-language offerings.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces Overall First-Look Deal with Colin Kaepernick
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced an overall first-look deal with Colin Kaepernick's production company, Ra Vision Media. This partnership will focus on developing scripted and unscripted stories exploring race, social injustice, and equity, while providing a platform for Black and Brown directors and producers across all Disney platforms. The first project in development is an exclusive docuseries chronicling Kaepernick's journey, utilizing new interviews and never-before-seen archives.

title: Why Disney wants to reopen its theme parks now
summary: Walt Disney World Resort in Florida is reopening amidst a surge in COVID-19 cases because other Disney enterprises like Disney+ and ESPN are not generating enough revenue. The company needs its theme parks, which serve as a crucial interactive PR tool and revenue source despite the pandemic's impact on other business segments. Disney has prior experience with reopening its Shanghai resort during the pandemic.

title: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® Elects Gilbert Dávila to Board of Directors
summary: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. (Nasdaq: CBRL) announced the election of Gilbert Dávila to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Mr. Dávila, founder and CEO of DMI Consulting, brings extensive experience in multicultural marketing, diversity & inclusion, market segmentation, and digital marketing from his leadership roles at The Walt Disney Company, Sears & Roebuck Company, Coca-Cola USA, and Procter & Gamble. This appointment supports Cracker Barrel's strategic focus on digital and multicultural engagement.

title: Disney Parks Boss ‘Pretty Pleased’ With Demand on Reopening Day
summary: Josh D’Amaro, chairman of Walt Disney Co.'s theme parks business, expressed satisfaction with booking trends as Magic Kingdom and Animal Kingdom reopened to the public after a four-month coronavirus shutdown. Disney is taking reservations through September 2021, with Epcot and Disney’s Hollywood Studios parks set to reopen later. This indicates strong initial demand for theme park visits following the reopening.

title: EA Sports UFC 4 coming in August on PS4 and Xbox One
summary: EA Sports UFC 4 is set to release on PS4 and Xbox One on August 14, featuring Jorge Masvidal and Israel Adesanya on the cover. The game will prioritize accessibility and expand beyond strict realism, particularly in its career mode and customization options. While no next-gen versions are confirmed, the Xbox One version will support Smart Delivery for Xbox Series X.

title: Disney+ Honored by American Council of the Blind for Achievement in Audio Description
summary: Disney+ has received the 2020 Achievement Award in Audio Description from the American Council of the Blind (ACB) for its commitment to providing audio description tracks for its original programming and extensive back catalog. The streaming service was recognized for its high standards in audio description scripts, quality voicing, and outreach to the blindness community. Disney+ is noted as the only streaming service with such a large number of titles available with audio description from its inception, showcasing The Walt Disney Company's long-standing dedication to accessibility.

title: Disney+ Honored by American Council of the Blind for Achievement in Audio Description
summary: Disney+ received the 2020 Achievement Award in Audio Description from the American Council of the Blind (ACB) for its commitment to adding audio description tracks to its entire slate of original programming and a significant portion of its back catalog. The service was recognized for its high standards in audio description scripts, quality voicing and audio mix, and outreach to the blindness community. Disney+ emphasizes accessibility and inclusiveness, treating it as an ongoing principle rather than a one-time project.

title: PepsiCo jumps after Cheetos-Hungry Americans stock up on comfort
summary: PepsiCo's sales surged due to increased at-home snacking on comfort foods like Tostitos, Fritos, and Cheetos during COVID-19 lockdowns, despite a decline in beverage sales. This article also covers Moderna's inclusion in the Nasdaq-100, Australia's push for tech giants to share revenue with news publishers, a strike at Bath Iron Works, RTW Retailwinds' bankruptcy, a projected fall in global coffee consumption, Southwest Airlines' warning of layoffs, Netflix surpassing Disney in market capitalization, Heathrow Airport closing a runway for repairs, and Huawei's sales growth despite restrictions.

title: Blerg, Most NBC Stations Won’t Air the 30 Rock Reunion
summary: Major NBC affiliate groups, including Gray Television and Sinclair Broadcast Group, have decided not to broadcast the upcoming 30 Rock reunion special, meaning about half the country won't see it when it debuts. The reason appears to be that station owners view the special, produced by NBCUniversal's ad-sales division, as too much of a promotion for the company’s new Peacock streaming platform. Despite the preemption, viewers in major markets will still be able to watch, and the special will be available on NBC.com, Peacock, and other NBCU cable networks.

title: NBCUniversal wades into streaming wars with Peacock
summary: NBCUniversal is launching its Peacock streaming service nationwide, offering a tiered service with free, ad-supported, and ad-free options. The company is betting on a hybrid model that includes news, sports, and a vast library of TV shows to differentiate itself from competitors like Netflix and Disney+. Peacock aims to attract consumers by replicating traditional TV economics while facing challenges like late entry into the streaming wars and distribution hurdles with major platforms.

title: Irving Azoff, Chairman and CEO, The Azoff Company
summary: Irving Azoff, Chairman and CEO of The Azoff Company, discusses the devastating impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the live music industry. He shares insights into how his company and artists are adapting, including the successful ESPN broadcast of an Eagles concert, and expresses pessimism about a full return to touring before summer 2021 due to economic and health uncertainties. Azoff emphasizes resilience and advises artists to protect their employees and crews.

title: Disney Executive Michael Colglazier Leaving Disney to Become CEO of Virgin Galactic
summary: Michael Colglazier, President and Managing Director of Disney Parks International, is leaving Disney to become Chief Executive Officer of Virgin Galactic Holdings, effective July 20th, 2020. Colglazier brings over thirty years of experience at Disney, including overseeing international parks and resorts and leading the Disneyland Resort during its 60th Anniversary. George Whitsides, Virgin Galactic's former CEO, will transition to Chief Space Officer, focusing on future business opportunities like hypersonic and orbital space travel.

title: Virgin Galactic hires Disney veteran as new CEO
summary: Virgin Galactic has appointed Michael Colglazier, a Walt Disney Company veteran, as its new CEO, effective July 20. Colglazier previously led Disney Parks International and was instrumental in the Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge expansion. Current CEO George Whitesides will transition to chief space officer, focusing on future business opportunities like hypersonic and orbital space travel.

title: NEWS! More Shakeups in the Walt Disney Company’s Leadership Team
summary: The Walt Disney Company is undergoing leadership changes with Michael Colglazier stepping down as Disney Parks International’s President and Managing Director to become Virgin Galactic’s new CEO. Additionally, Jackie Swisher has replaced Phil Holmes as the Vice President of Disney’s Hollywood Studios. These shifts follow Bob Chapek's recent appointment as CEO of The Walt Disney Company.

title: Abigail Disney slams Disney World reopening as coronavirus spreads
summary: Walt Disney Co. heiress Abigail Disney has criticized the reopening of Disney World amidst the ongoing coronavirus pandemic, expressing concern for the health and safety of workers and guests. She also reiterated her earlier criticisms regarding executive compensation and the furloughing of park employees, suggesting executives should have forgone pay to support workers. The article details Disney's safety measures for reopening, as well as the indefinite delay of Disneyland's reopening in California.

title: Barr condemns Disney and Hollywood for 'kowtowing' to China | William Barr
summary: US Attorney General William Barr criticized Disney and other Hollywood studios for allegedly "kowtowing" to the Chinese Communist Party, accusing them of prioritizing short-term profits over American values. Barr highlighted instances where Disney reportedly apologized for a film about the Dalai Lama and allowed Chinese officials a role in Shanghai Disneyland, while Hollywood studios allegedly tweaked scripts to appease Beijing. He also extended his criticism to US technology companies, calling them "pawns of Chinese influence" for their operations in China.

title: Virgin Galactic announces Michael Colglazier as CEO
summary: Virgin Galactic announced the appointment of Michael Colglazier as its new chief executive officer and George Whitesides as chief space officer, effective July 20, 2020. Colglazier, formerly of The Walt Disney Company, brings extensive experience in consumer-oriented multi-billion dollar businesses. Whitesides, the former CEO, will focus on future business opportunities like hypersonic and orbital space travel, while also chairing the company's space advisory board.

title: Summer Blockbusters Were Slated for This Weekend. Most People Aren’t Ready to Go Back to the Movies
summary: New polling data indicates that between two-thirds and three-quarters of adults in every U.S. state are uncomfortable returning to movie theaters, despite Hollywood's plans to release major blockbusters. Experts suggest that opening theaters prematurely could be detrimental, as low audience comfort combined with increased operating costs from safety measures would lead to razor-thin profit margins. The industry faces significant challenges, including staggered reopenings across states and studios' unwillingness to release big films if returns are low, highlighting a complex interplay between government regulations, studio decisions, and audience readiness.

title: Slideshow: What’s new from General Mills, Kellogg, Three Wishes
summary: General Mills, Kellogg Co., and Three Wishes Cereal are introducing new ready-to-eat cereal products. General Mills is launching a Mandalorian-themed cereal, Kellogg is releasing a Mashups Cereal combining Frosted Flakes and Froot Loops, and Three Wishes is expanding its grain-free portfolio with a new cocoa flavor. These innovations aim to cater to diverse consumer preferences in the breakfast cereal market.

title: Looking for an escape: Younger people more likely to say entertainment costs rose since COVID-19
summary: A global Ipsos survey reveals that a quarter of people in 26 countries believe entertainment costs (electronics, movies, books) have increased since COVID-19, with younger individuals (under 35) being most likely to report this. The article highlights the boom in streaming services and gaming during the pandemic, noting that companies quickly adapted to deliver content to homes. While some changes in consumer behavior, like higher Premium VOD use, are expected to persist, there are concerns about content production shutdowns and "streaming fatigue."

title: U.S. Attorney General Accuses The Walt Disney Company of "Kowtowing" to Chinese Government; 300 of Shanghai Disneyland's Cast Members Active Members of Communist Party
summary: U.S. Attorney General William Barr accused The Walt Disney Company of "kowtowing" to the Chinese government, citing the presence of 300 active Communist Party members among Shanghai Disneyland's 11,000 employees and the Chinese government's role in managing the resort. Barr also referenced Disney's past apology for the film "Kundun" and the company's efforts to appeal to the Chinese film market, which generated significant revenue. Disney has not commented on Barr's remarks.

title: Fortune 500 Tapestry CEO Jide Zeitlin Quits For Personal Reasons After Less Than A Year On Job
summary: Jide Zeitlin, CEO of Fortune 500 Tapestry Inc., resigned for personal reasons after less than a year, amidst allegations of an inappropriate personal relationship predating his tenure. His departure reduces the number of Black CEOs in Fortune 500 companies to three. Zeitlin had also been a vocal advocate against racism and for Black Lives Matter.

title: Fox Will Fill Empty Baseball Stadiums With Virtual Fans
summary: Fox Sports plans to use virtual fans to fill seats in MLB stadiums during its broadcasts to create a more traditional viewing experience amidst the coronavirus pandemic. This digital augmentation will allow for custom crowd reactions and appearances, aiming to make games look and sound authentic despite empty stands. The move is a response to the challenge faced by broadcasters in making sports look appealing without live audiences, with other networks exploring similar innovations.

title: AT&T calls launch of streamer HBO Max a success despite business challenges posed by COVID-19
summary: AT&T declared the launch of HBO Max a success despite COVID-19 challenges, with 4.1 million subscribers in its first month and targets for 50 million by 2025. The service's broad content and existing library attracted customers despite initial delays in original series production caused by the pandemic. While revenue across AT&T's businesses fell due to COVID-19, HBO Max's performance was a positive note, though big theatrical releases like "Tenet" are still planned for cinemas.

title: Streaming service Philo adds TV One to lineup, won't raise price
summary: Philo is adding TV One to its lineup of 60 pay TV networks, making it the first time the channel is available without a traditional cable or satellite subscription. This addition is part of Philo's commitment to diverse programming and will not result in a price increase for customers, maintaining its $20 a month subscription package. The move also benefits Urban One, as Philo becomes the first streaming cable TV alternative to offer both TV One and Cleo TV in its basic package.

title: Disney Company Acquisitions: The Miramax Deal
summary: This article details The Walt Disney Company's acquisition of Miramax in 1993, highlighting it as one of Disney's first major acquisitions aimed at expanding into non-family-friendly content for young adults. It explores the tumultuous relationship between Disney and Miramax founders Bob and Harvey Weinstein due to creative differences and financial disputes, ultimately leading to Miramax's sale in 2010. The piece evaluates the acquisition as a learning opportunity for Disney, paving the way for future major deals under Iger, despite its own challenges.

title: 'Tenet' to hit international theaters on Aug. 26, some U.S. cinemas over Labor Day weekend
summary: Christopher Nolan's "Tenet" will have a staggered release, debuting internationally on August 26, 2020, followed by a limited release in select U.S. cities over Labor Day weekend. This unusual strategy aims to recoup its substantial budget and support international theaters, as Hollywood blockbusters often generate a significant portion of their revenue from overseas markets. The domestic movie theater industry has been severely impacted by the coronavirus pandemic, leading to multiple delays for anticipated blockbusters like "Tenet" and "Mulan."

title: Disney Launchpad: Shorts Incubator Unveils 2020 Directors
summary: Disney Launchpad: Shorts Incubator, a program aimed at amplifying underrepresented voices, has announced its six directors for the inaugural 2020 year: Ann Marie Pace, Aqsa Altaf, Hao Zheng, Jessica Mendez Siqueiros, Moxie Peng, and Stefanie Abel Horowitz. These directors will develop original live-action short films centered on the theme "Discover," with the potential for their works to be featured on Disney+. The program provides mentorship, script development, and classes, with the ultimate goal of empowering a new generation of filmmakers and reflecting diverse global perspectives.

title: James Murdoch resigns from news publisher News Corp’s board
summary: James Murdoch, son of News Corp founder Rupert Murdoch, has resigned from the company's board, citing disagreements over editorial content and strategic decisions. He is known as the more liberal Murdoch brother, contrasting with his conservative sibling Lachlan, who is co-chairman of News Corp and CEO of Fox Corp. James has previously criticized News Corp's editorial stance, including its outlets' coverage of climate change.

title: Rupert Murdoch’s Son James Resigns From News Corp. Due To ‘Disagreements’
summary: James Murdoch, the youngest son of Rupert Murdoch, resigned from the News Corp. board, citing "disagreements over certain editorial content" and "strategic decisions." This marks his final departure from formal roles within his family’s media empire. Murdoch had previously criticized the family's news outlets for their stance on climate change and has supported Democratic candidates and sustainability causes.

title: James Murdoch cuts ties with father Rupert’s News Corp empire
summary: James Murdoch has resigned from the board of his father Rupert Murdoch's News Corp., citing "disagreements over certain editorial content" and strategic decisions. This move further distances him from the conservative-leaning media empire, particularly after recent tensions over the Wall Street Journal's opinion section. Murdoch, who said he doesn't watch Fox News, has been critical of the company's coverage of issues like global warming and is pursuing investments through his firm Lupa Systems that counter the family's main media outlets.

title: Here’s how PayPal hopes to turn Venmo into the next PayPal
summary: PayPal is looking to increase revenue from its Venmo brand, which is popular with younger consumers, by introducing new features like a credit card. Darrell Esch, the new general manager of Venmo, is tasked with leading this initiative as digital wallets become increasingly important. PayPal itself has experienced significant growth during the COVID-19 pandemic, surpassing the market capitalization of several major companies.

title: 16 AMC Cinemas locations to offer Dolby experience in KSA
summary: AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc. and Dolby Laboratories, Inc. announced a partnership to bring the Dolby Cinema experience to 16 AMC Cinemas locations in Saudi Arabia over the next four years, with the first expected by the end of 2020. This expansion aims to provide moviegoers with a premium experience featuring Dolby Vision's ultravivid picture and Dolby Atmos' immersive sound. AMC plans to significantly increase its presence in Saudi Arabia, with eight new sites by the end of 2020 and an additional 14 in 2021.

title: Live-action 'Mulan' will be released on Disney+ for added $29.99
summary: Disney announced that its live-action "Mulan" film will bypass a major theatrical release and instead debut on Disney+ on September 4th. Subscribers will need to pay an additional $29.99 to rent the film, beyond their monthly subscription. This decision was made to bring the family-friendly film to a broad audience during an unpredictable period when many cannot go to movie theaters.

title: 'Mulan' will now premiere on Disney Plus for $30
summary: Disney announced that its live-action "Mulan" will premiere on Disney+ for an additional $29.99 on September 4, bypassing a major theatrical release due to the coronavirus pandemic. This decision comes as Disney reported a significant net income drop in the last quarter, largely due to theme park closures and movie postponements, though its streaming service continued to grow with 57.5 million paid subscribers by June 27. The company views this streaming release as an opportunity to reach a broad audience unable to attend cinemas.

title: NBCUniversal Chairman Steve Burke Extends Comcast Deal As Advisor
summary: NBCUniversal chairman and former CEO Steve Burke has extended his tenure with parent company Comcast, transitioning from chairman to a senior adviser role beginning January 2021. His new contract runs through 2025, paying him $350,000 annually for the part-time position, with stipulations against working for other companies. This move follows a common practice at Comcast of retaining top executives in advisory capacities after they step down from their primary roles.

title: Disney Parks Pandemic Closures Result in $3.5 Billion Loss
summary: The Walt Disney Co. announced a $3.5 billion loss in its fiscal third quarter due to the closure of its theme parks worldwide caused by the novel coronavirus pandemic. Parks, Experiences and Products revenues decreased by 85 percent to $1.0 billion, resulting in a $2.0 billion operating loss for the segment. While Disney World in Florida has reopened, Disneyland in California remains largely closed, with its reopening dependent on state guidelines.

title: BREAKING: Parks, Experiences and Products Loses $2 Billion in Third Quarter, The Walt Disney Company Reports Historic Losses in Revenue Due to COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a significant revenue loss in its Q3 FY20 earnings report, primarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Parks, Experiences and Products segment alone lost $2.0 billion, impacting overall revenue which was down 41.8% year-over-year to $11.78 billion. Despite the financial setbacks in its physical parks, Disney's streaming services, Disney+ and ESPN+, showed strong subscriber growth during the quarter.

title: Disney Quarterly Earnings: Parks Lose $2 Billion, WDW Attendance Down & More
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported its Q3 2020 earnings, revealing significant losses, especially for the Parks, Resorts & Experiences division, which lost $2 billion. Despite a revenue decrease of 42% year-over-year, Disney's stock saw an after-hours bump, and Disney+ exceeded revised subscriber expectations, reaching 60.5 million. The company is weathering the financial storm with $23 billion in cash and is adapting to challenges, including lower-than-expected Walt Disney World attendance, by optimizing operations despite reduced CapEx and potential long-term recovery in destination travel.

title: Powering the Magic with Renewable Energy
summary: The Walt Disney Company is making continuous investments in renewable energy across its global operations to achieve its long-term goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions. This includes expanding solar arrays at corporate campuses, utilizing geothermal energy at Disneyland Paris, and opening a new 270-acre solar facility near Walt Disney World Resort capable of powering two theme parks. These efforts highlight Disney's commitment to clean electricity and increasing its renewable energy portfolio.

title: Novavax Stock Soars, Beyond Meat Drops and the Dow Keeps Marching Higher
summary: U.S. markets saw widespread gains as investors processed new earnings reports and monitored discussions in Washington regarding the next COVID-19 relief package. Novavax shares surged following positive clinical trial results for its Covid-19 vaccine, while Beyond Meat's stock fell due to higher-than-expected pandemic-related costs despite beating financial estimates. Disney and CVS Health also reported stronger-than-anticipated results, contributing to the overall market optimism.

title: Power Moves | Condé Nast Entertainment Hires President From Walt Disney Company, Gucci Global Head of Diversity Departs
summary: Condé Nast Entertainment has hired Agnes Chu, previously from Walt Disney Company, as its new president. Renée Tirado, Gucci's global head of diversity, equity, and inclusion, has departed to launch her own consulting firm. The article also highlights other significant executive appointments and departures in the fashion and media industries.

title: Judge Approves Ending Paramount Antitrust Consent Decrees
summary: A federal judge has approved the Justice Department's request to end the Paramount Consent Decrees, which previously barred movie studios from owning theaters. These antitrust rules, in place since the golden age of cinema, are now considered anachronistic given the rise of streaming and the challenges facing movie theaters. The decision is not expected to significantly alter Hollywood's business landscape, though it will eventually remove restrictions on "block booking" and "circuit dealing" after a two-year sunset period.

title: Walt Disney World to Reduce Theme Park Hours Next Month
