summary: Netflix's continuous production of hit shows is positioning it strongly in the competitive streaming market, leading analysts to predict double-digit revenue growth later this year. Following a strong fourth quarter where it surpassed subscriber addition estimates, Netflix shares surged. The company plans to implement features this quarter to convert password sharers into paying subscribers and grow its ad-supported tier.

title: ‘Avatar: The Way of Water’ Crosses $2 Billion Worldwide
summary: Six weeks after its release, 20th Century Studios’ Avatar: The Way of Water has surpassed $2 billion at the global box office, making it only the sixth film in history to achieve this milestone. Director James Cameron now has three of the top six highest-grossing films globally, with the original Avatar still holding the No. 1 spot. The film is the highest-grossing global release of 2022 and of the pandemic era.

title: Rival Orlando Theme Park Takes Shot at Disney Adults Over Splash Mountain Closure
summary: SeaWorld Orlando seized an opportunity to playfully mock "Disney Adults" following the closure of Splash Mountain at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom. As Disney fans expressed sadness over the attraction's retheming, SeaWorld posted a tweet referencing "splashing" to remind guests of other water ride options. This highlights the competitive nature among Orlando theme parks.

title: The Walt Disney Company Leads All Studios With 22 Academy Award Nominations
summary: The Walt Disney Company received a total of 22 Academy Award nominations for the upcoming 95th Oscars ceremony, leading all studios. Key nominations include "Avatar: The Way of Water" and "The Banshees of Inisherin" for Best Picture, with the latter securing nine nominations and "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" receiving five. Other recognized films include "Empire of Light," "Fire of Love," "Le Pupille," and "Turning Red."

title: Jakks Pacific announces its first set of toys for The Super Mario Bros. Movie
summary: Jakks Pacific has revealed its first line of toys for The Super Mario Bros. Movie, featuring 5-inch figures of Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Toad with acrylic eyes. More toys are anticipated as the movie's February 26th release date approaches. Jakks Pacific has a long-standing relationship with Nintendo, handling various properties.

title: Rupert Murdoch drops Fox-News Corp merger plan
summary: Rupert Murdoch has decided to halt plans for merging Fox Corporation and News Corp, a move announced by both companies. The proposed merger faced skepticism from Wall Street and opposition from an activist hedge fund, which argued against the financial sense and synergies of the deal. Murdoch, 91, had reportedly considered the merger as part of succession planning, but investors preferred other strategic alternatives for News Corp.

title: Billionaires Worth $123 Billion Buy Stake In Kushner’s Thrive
summary: A group of global billionaires, collectively worth at least $123 billion, are investing in Thrive Capital, the venture-capital firm founded by Josh Kushner. Notable investors include Mukesh Ambani, Jorge Paulo Lemann, Xavier Niel, Henry Kravis, and Robert Iger, who are together purchasing a 3.3% stake in Thrive for $175 million.

title: Super Mario Bros. Movie Toys Offer Hi-Res Looks at Peach, Toad and Luigi
summary: JAKKS Pacific has partnered with Illumination and Nintendo to release a new line of merchandise for The Super Mario Bros. Movie, featuring posable figures of characters like Peach, Luigi, Mario, and Toad. These new toys, which offer detailed looks at the characters, are set to be released on February 26th. The article also touches on previous toy-related reveals and the casting controversy surrounding Chris Pratt as Mario.

title: Mattel Is Making Disney Princess Dolls Again
summary: Mattel has regained the license to produce Disney Princess dolls nearly a decade after losing it to Hasbro. This comeback signifies a major triumph for Mattel, following years of financial struggles and creative stagnation. The company plans to introduce new designs for the dolls, focusing on making them more representative of how children perceive the characters, and this initiative is part of a broader effort to revitalize Mattel's design approach and overall business.

title: Comcast Corp. nods to new Frisco park and sees ‘great momentum’ in theme parks business
summary: Comcast Corp. highlighted its new kids-oriented Universal theme park planned for Frisco and a horror attraction for Las Vegas during its quarterly financial results call. CEO Brian Roberts stated these new parks are innovative ways to utilize their intellectual properties from DreamWorks and Illumination, extending the brand and fueling growth across all Universal parks. The company saw a significant 49.3% increase in theme park revenue last year, reaching $7.5 billion, and anticipates continued momentum in this sector.

title: Disneyland, California Adventure celebrating Disney's 100th anniversary with several new attractions, shows
summary: Disneyland and Disney California Adventure are kicking off celebrations for the Walt Disney Co.'s 100th anniversary with new attractions, decor, merchandise, and entertainment. Highlights include the opening of Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway, and two new nighttime spectaculars: "Wondrous Journeys" at Disneyland and "World of Color -- ONE" at Disney California Adventure. The resorts are adorned with platinum-infused décor, and special exhibitions detail Walt Disney's vision.

title: Momo to swim in global waters with Bejuba!
summary: Canadian distributor Bejuba! Entertainment has acquired the global distribution rights for iQIYI's preschool series "Momo," excluding China. The 2D-animated show, featuring a young octopus and her father, is currently in its second season of production. "Momo" was created by Wang Huiyu of iQIYI’s Wonderworks division, with an international team contributing to its animation and scriptwriting.

title: This is likely the real reason some cruise lines are returning to in-person muster drills
summary: Norwegian Cruise Line is returning to mandatory in-person muster drills, citing safety, but other major cruise lines like Royal Caribbean and Carnival continue to praise e-mustering for its safety and guest experience improvements. The move by Norwegian comes amidst significant cost-cutting and fee increases across its operations, leading to speculation that staffing costs for e-mustering are the real reason for the change, rather than safety concerns. Other cruise lines, including Disney, Oceania, and Regent Seven Seas, have also reverted to in-person drills.

title: Alliance Entertainment’s Mill Creek Entertainment Announces New Home Entertainment Licensing Agreement with The Walt Disney Company
summary: Mill Creek Entertainment, a division of Alliance Entertainment Holding Corporation, has signed a multi-year home entertainment licensing agreement with The Walt Disney Company. This agreement will allow Distribution Solutions, another division of Alliance Entertainment, to distribute hundreds of select physical Blu-ray and DVD titles from various Disney content libraries. The partnership aims to expand the availability of Disney's live-action film and television properties to collectors and fans through Mill Creek's network of retailers.

title: ‘Avatar: The Way of Water’ Is the 4th Highest-Grossing Film of All-Time
summary: Avatar: The Way of Water has become the fourth highest-grossing film worldwide, surpassing Star Wars: The Force Awakens. It is also the second fastest film to reach $2 billion and is nominated for four Academy Awards, including Best Picture. James Cameron has directed three of the top four grossing films of all time; Avatar, Titanic, and Avatar: The Way of Water.

title: Banana Boat sunscreen recall expanded over benzene concerns
summary: Edgewell Personal Care Company has expanded its recall of Banana Boat Hair & Scalp Sunscreen Spray SPF 30 to include an additional batch, bringing the total to four batches, due to the presence of the cancer-causing chemical benzene. The benzene is linked to the product's propellant, not an ingredient in the sunscreen itself. Although no adverse events have been reported, the company has notified retailers and is offering reimbursements to consumers.

title: Netflix Inc. stock rises Tuesday, still underperforms market
summary: Netflix Inc. stock saw a modest increase of 0.21% on Tuesday, closing at $353.86, despite a strong day for the broader market with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also rising. The stock's performance underperformed compared to competitors like Apple, Walt Disney, and Comcast, and it remained significantly below its 52-week high. Trading volume was also notably lower than its 50-day average.

title: Disney Remains Most-Admired Media and Entertainment Company
summary: For the 20th consecutive year, The Walt Disney Company has been recognized as the top-ranked media and entertainment company on Fortune’s annual "World’s Most Admired Companies" list. Disney ranked No. 6 overall among 324 listed companies, earning high marks in areas such as innovation, social responsibility, financial soundness, and quality of products and services. The list was compiled by Fortune and Korn Ferry, surveying executives, directors, and analysts.

title: We Finally Know Where 'Westworld' Will be Available to Stream
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery has announced that several of its series, including "Westworld," will be available on Free, Ad-Based Television (FAST) streamers Tubi and Roku. This move comes after the company's merger led to cancellations and removals from HBO Max. While ads may be present, this offers a free alternative for viewers and could benefit FAST streamers by adding high-profile content to their libraries.

title: 10 Companies Who Inspire Creative Team Collaboration
summary: This article highlights ten companies that excel at fostering creative team collaboration. It explains how these businesses, ranging from tech giants like Google and Amazon to entertainment powerhouses like Disney and Blizzard Entertainment, prioritize open communication, diverse perspectives, and inclusive environments to drive innovation and achieve shared goals. The article emphasizes that creative collaboration is crucial for developing new ideas and products, leading to a sense of shared ownership and motivation among team members.

title: Netflix deletes new rules on account sharing after public outrage, says US customers yet to be affected
summary: Netflix deleted new rules regarding account sharing from its website after facing significant public backlash. The company clarified that the detailed rules, which sparked outrage, were mistakenly updated for countries outside of Chile, Costa Rica, and Peru, where they are already in place. Although the company still plans to introduce account sharing restrictions for U.S. customers by March 2023, the exact nature of these rules remains unclear following the controversy.

title: Gov. DeSantis targets Reedy Creek. 10 things to know about the Disney-run tax district
summary: Florida legislators are holding a special session this week, with Gov. Ron DeSantis targeting Walt Disney World's Reedy Creek Improvement District for major changes. DeSantis' plan would give control of the district to a state-controlled board appointed by the governor, ending Disney's self-governance. This move stems from a clash between DeSantis and Disney following the company's opposition to the governor's parental rights legislation.

title: AT&T Inc. stock falls Monday, underperforms market
summary: AT&T Inc. (T) stock dropped 1.26% on Monday to $19.58, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also saw declines. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for AT&T, bringing its share price $3.26 below its 52-week high. The stock also underperformed against competitors such as Netflix, Walt Disney Co., and Comcast Corp. Class A.

title: Magnite Unveils Magnite Streaming, New Ad Platform For CTV and OTT | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: Magnite has launched "Magnite Streaming," a new ad platform designed to help media owners monetize advertising inventory in live and on-demand connected TV (CTV) and over-the-top (OTT) video. The platform integrates technology from Magnite CTV and SpotX, offering comprehensive seller deal management, inventory curation, audience activation, and advanced reporting. This initiative responds to the growing consumer adoption of ad-supported streaming services and aims to provide a unified solution for media owners like AMC Networks and Warner Bros. Discovery to optimize their ad strategies.

title: Q4 Corporate Earnings Moving In Opposite Direction of Economic Indicators
summary: Q4 S&P 500 corporate earnings growth is lagging, currently at -5.3% YoY, even as economic indicators show positive momentum. Big tech misses from Meta, Alphabet, Amazon, and Apple contributed to the decline, though some companies like Meta were rewarded for cost-cutting. Despite lower-than-average estimate beats, guidance has been better than expected, contrasting with robust economic data like Q4 GDP growth and strong non-farm payrolls.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Third Point Has a Stake in Salesforce
summary: Dan Loeb’s Third Point LLC has acquired a stake in Salesforce Inc., according to sources, making it the fifth activist shareholder to invest in the software company. Third Point is known for pushing for changes at major companies, having previously targeted Campbell Soup Co., Shell PLC, and Walt Disney Co. This move signals increasing activist interest in Salesforce's shares.

title: Bob Iger announces 7,000 job cuts at Disney, signals ‘significant transformation’
summary: Walt Disney Co. CEO Bob Iger announced 7,000 job cuts and $5.5 billion in cost savings, signaling a significant transformation for the company amidst challenges in streaming economics and an uncertain economic environment. The move comes as Disney+ continues to lose money, despite the company exceeding Wall Street estimates in its fiscal first quarter earnings. The restructuring will divide Disney into three units: Disney Entertainment, ESPN, and Disney Parks, Experiences and Products.

title: $82.4 Billion Worldwide Amusement and Theme Parks Industry
summary: A new report by Research and Markets projects the global amusement and theme parks industry to grow from US$54.9 Billion in 2022 to US$82.4 Billion by 2030, exhibiting a CAGR of 5.2%. This growth is driven by consumer incomes and a desire for recreational activities, with mechanical rides and water rides identified as key segments. The U.S. market leads, while China is expected to show the highest growth rate.

title: Disney Details Strategic Restructuring; Dana Walden, Alan Bergman to Oversee Both Disney+ and Hulu in New Roles
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced a major strategic restructuring aimed at centralizing creativity and enhancing accountability among its leaders. This plan organizes the company into three core segments: Disney Entertainment, ESPN, and Disney Parks, Experiences and Products (DPEP), giving segment leaders full operational and financial control. Notably, Dana Walden and Alan Bergman will jointly oversee the streaming strategy for both Disney+ and Hulu, in addition to their expanded roles within Disney Entertainment.

title: Media & Entertainment - Social Media Ranking by Engagement in India
summary: The Indian Media & Entertainment industry is experiencing significant growth, with over 514 million cross-platform actions on major social media platforms in January 2023. This report ranks the top 12 properties in India by engagement, highlighting Aaj Tak, ABP News, and STAR Vijay Television as leaders. The article emphasizes the increasing importance of social media for publishers to understand audience connection and define monetization strategies.

title: Disney stock rises as CEO Bob Iger unveils transformation plan
summary: Disney's stock is at a five-month high after its Q1 earnings beat expectations, driven by strong performance in theme parks and shrinking streaming losses, despite a subscriber drop for Disney+. CEO Bob Iger announced a "significant transformation" plan to restructure divisions, cut 7,000 jobs to reduce expenses by $5.5 billion annually, and resume dividend payments. The plan aims to maximize creative potential, improve efficiency, and make streaming profitable, leading to a positive market reaction and potentially settling concerns from activist investors.

title: Wall St dips as Treasury yields rise after auction
summary: U.S. stock indexes closed lower on Thursday, reversing earlier gains as Treasury yields increased after a poorly received auction of 30-year bonds. This overshadowed strong earnings reports from companies like Disney and PepsiCo. Weak demand for the $21 billion sale of 30-year Treasury bonds led to a rise in yields, making bonds a more attractive alternative to equities for investors.

title: Disney’s Layoffs and Restructuring Shows Parents Don’t Want ‘Woke’ Entertainment
summary: The Walt Disney Co. announced a significant restructuring, including 7,000 layoffs and $5.5 billion in cost cuts, largely attributed to losses in its streaming division and underperforming "woke" films. CEO Bob Iger stated the changes aim to return creativity to the company, improve financial results, and ensure content quality. The article suggests this move could be a response to audience pushback against ideologically driven content in children's entertainment, citing box office failures of movies like "Lightyear" and "Strange World."

title: Disney plans to follow Florida’s rules for Reedy Creek takeover, company says
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced its intention to comply with Florida's new legislation regarding the Reedy Creek Improvement District, which will transition into a state-controlled "Central Florida Tourism Oversight District." This decision comes after a period of dispute between Disney and the state over Florida's Parental Rights in Education law. Walt Disney World Resort President Jeff Vahle stated that the company is focused on the future and will work within the new framework.

title: Molson Coors’ Super Bowl Swerve Highlights Blue Moon; Heineken and Marvel Partner for NA Beer’s First Big Game Spot
summary: Molson Coors surprised Super Bowl viewers by making its first national ad in over 30 years a Blue Moon commercial, despite a highly-teased battle between Coors Light and Miller Lite. The campaign generated significant media impressions and high rankings in ad lists. Separately, Heineken 0.0 partnered with Marvel for the first non-alcoholic beer Super Bowl ad, featuring Paul Rudd as Ant-Man. Anheuser-Busch also aired multiple national spots, and Boston Beer Company’s Samuel Adams ran a notable regional ad.

title: Fubo TV restores monthly billing option for new members
summary: Fubo TV has reinstated its monthly billing option for new subscribers, although the sign-up process still defaults to quarterly. The company previously moved to a three-month billing cycle, which was seen as an undesirable change for customers. This update comes amidst additional complexities for Fubo TV users, including the introduction of new Regional Sports Fees ranging from $11 to $14 per month, regardless of whether a subscriber wants these channels.

title: Comcast Corp. Cl A stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA) shares dropped by 0.08% on Tuesday, closing at $39.06, underperforming the broader market. This decline broke a two-day winning streak for the stock, placing it $9.36 below its 52-week high. Competitors such as Netflix Inc. (NFLX) saw gains, while Walt Disney Co. (DIS) and Charter Communications Inc. Cl A (CHTR) remained unchanged.

title: Ally and Disney create unprecedented media and collegiate collaboration to advance parity for women's sports
summary: Ally Financial Inc. and The Walt Disney Company have announced a multi-year, multimillion-dollar investment to advance equality in women's sports coverage. This unprecedented collaboration will see over 90% of the media investment focused on women's sports across ESPN networks and includes Ally becoming an official sponsor of the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) with title sponsorships for women's basketball and soccer championships. The initiative aims to change traditional media buying practices, increase visibility, and create systemic change to level the playing field for female athletes.

title: How Bally Sports' Financial Troubles Could Impact Sports Fans, Teams and Leagues
summary: Diamond Sports Group, the owner of Bally Sports channels, skipped a significant debt payment, signaling potential financial distress including a possible Chapter 11 bankruptcy. This situation could severely impact professional sports leagues like MLB, NBA, and NHL, which rely on Bally Sports for local broadcasting rights and revenue. Leagues are already developing contingency plans to ensure game availability for fans, exploring options for digital and linear TV distribution if Diamond Sports Group fails.

title: Netflix plunges after the streaming giant launches a wave of price cuts in 100 countries in the face of stiff competition
summary: Netflix's stock dropped 5% on Thursday following reports that the company is implementing significant price cuts across over 100 countries, affecting more than 10 million subscribers. These price reductions, some as high as 50%, mark a shift from Netflix's previous strategy of raising prices and come amid increased competition in the streaming market and efforts to curb password sharing. The company aims to improve member experience and offer more affordable options, as evidenced by its recent ad-supported subscription tier.

title: New Mattel Theme Park Might Compete With Disney
summary: Mattel is set to open a new theme park in Glendale, Arizona, in partnership with Epic Resort Destinations, featuring attractions based on popular brands like Barbie, Hot Wheels, and Thomas & Friends. The park aims to offer immersive experiences similar to those found at Disney and Universal, with features like a double-looping Hot Wheels coaster, a Barbie Beach House, and a Masters of the Universe laser tag arena. This new venture is anticipated to compete with established theme park giants, prompting Disney and Universal to invest in their own new projects.

title: Step-By-Step Guide To Opening A moomoo Account
summary: This article provides a step-by-step guide to opening a moomoo securities account, highlighting the ease and speed of the process. It covers downloading the app, filling in details, waiting for confirmation, and funding the account, while also mentioning moomoo's value-added services like paper trading and a worldwide investment community. The guide aims to encourage both new and experienced Singaporean investors to try the moomoo platform due to its low trading fees and useful features.

title: Third Point’s Dan Loeb pens a pointed letter to Bath & Body Works – What could happen next
summary: Third Point, led by Dan Loeb, has sent a strong letter to Bath & Body Works' board, expressing concerns about corporate governance, executive compensation, and shareholder rights. The activist investor intends to nominate a slate of director candidates amidst controversy surrounding former interim CEO Sarah Nash's $18 million compensation package for seven months of work. Third Point believes additional board oversight is necessary and contrasts BBWI's compensation practices with those of other large companies and their activist-involved boards.

title: These Billionaire Owners Of Luxury Hotels Plan To Start Cruise Ship Operators
summary: Luxury hotel brands like Ritz-Carlton and Four Seasons, along with new entrants like Aman Resorts, are expanding into high-end cruising, targeting wealthy travelers. This move comes as existing cruise operators struggle with pandemic-incurred debt and lower occupancy, while luxury travel recovers faster. The new ventures aim to leverage brand recognition and existing loyalty programs, creating competition for the higher-spending customer segment.

title: Union Pacific CEO to step down as hedge fund presses for change
summary: Union Pacific announced that CEO Lance Fritz will step down in 2023, following pressure from hedge fund Soroban Capital Partners. Soroban, which holds a $1.6 billion stake, had called for Fritz's replacement to improve operational efficiency and suggested former COO Jim Vena as a strong candidate. The company's board is seeking a new CEO both internally and externally, having considered shareholder input, and aims to find a leader for a long-term tenure.

title: Disney100: Vera Bradley Fairytale Collection Brings Wonder and Whimsy to shopDisney
summary: Vera Bradley is launching a new Fairytale-themed collection on shopDisney to celebrate Disney's 100th anniversary. The collection, available starting March 1st, features brightly colored flowers and classic Disney characters like Snow White, Bambi, and Winnie the Pooh on various bags and accessories. Fans can expect items such as totes, backpacks, crossbody bags, and cosmetic cases.

title: Disney+ Debuts ‘Peter Pan & Wendy’ Trailer
summary: Disney+ has released the trailer for its live-action film "Peter Pan & Wendy," which is a reimagining of the classic J.M. Barrie novel and the 1953 animated movie. The film will begin streaming on April 28, 2023, and features a star-studded cast, with director David Lowery aiming to honor both the original text and Walt Disney's adaptation while bringing emotional sincerity and a sense of adventure to the story.

title: Smartly.io Makes Strategic C-Suite Addition, Welcoming Snap and Facebook Veteran Brett Wein as Chief Sales Officer
summary: Smartly.io, a leading digital advertising platform, has appointed Brett Wein as its new Chief Sales Officer. Wein, a veteran in media and adtech with over a decade of sales leadership experience at Snap and Facebook, will be responsible for driving global growth and leading sales and strategic partnerships. His extensive background is expected to strengthen Smartly.io's position in the evolving digital advertising landscape.

title: Televisa llega a un acuerdo para resolver demanda en torno a derechos de Mundiales
summary: Grupo Televisa SAB has reached a preliminary agreement to settle a lawsuit filed by a U.S. investor for $95 million. The lawsuit accused the Mexican broadcaster of bribing FIFA officials to secure broadcasting rights for four World Cups. Televisa denied any wrongdoing, and the settlement still requires approval from a federal judge.

title: Could Liberty Media buy into Liverpool FC?
summary: Fenway Sports Group (FSG) is seeking a strategic partner for a minority stake in Liverpool FC, with The Telegraph identifying Liberty Media as a potential investor. While Liberty Media's ownership of the Atlanta Braves and Sirius XM (which broadcasts Premier League matches) presents potential conflicts of interest, their existing focus on racing in sports and access to LeBron James through FSG's investments make a collaboration attractive. The article suggests that an investment from Liberty Media could provide increased funding for Liverpool and allow Liberty to capitalize on rising Premier League media rights fees.

title: How Gen Z favorite E.l.f. cosmetics became an entertainment powerhouse
summary: E.l.f. Cosmetics has transformed into an entertainment powerhouse by leveraging innovative digital campaigns, strategic partnerships, and platform launches to engage its Gen Z audience. Beyond selling affordable beauty products, E.l.f. focuses on user-generated content, influencer collaborations, and experimental marketing to attract and entertain its 14 million social media followers, positioning itself as both a beauty brand and an entertainment company.

title: Royal Caribbean Group stock rises Thursday, still underperforms market
summary: Royal Caribbean Group stock saw a modest increase of 0.66% on Thursday, closing at $71.97. Despite this gain, the stock underperformed the broader market, as both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more significantly. The company's shares are still $15.71 below its 52-week high.

title: Fresh Del Monte Produce Announces Collaboration With DreamWorks Animation and Netflix; Pablo Rivero Comments
summary: Fresh Del Monte Produce has partnered with DreamWorks Animation and Netflix for a promotional collaboration featuring the "Kung Fu Panda: The Dragon Knight" series. This initiative aims to encourage children to consume more fruits and vegetables by adding character graphics to select product packaging, including Del Monte Gold® Pineapple, Honeyglow® Pineapple, and Del Monte® Bananas. Consumers in the U.S. and Canada also have the chance to win a family trip to Universal Studios Hollywood.

title: Despite Carriage Dispute Keeping CBS Stations Off Fubo TV, Nexstar President Tom Carter Expects Bundle Revenue To Keep Flowing: “We Do Not See A Cliff”
summary: Despite a carriage dispute with FuboTV affecting its CBS stations, Nexstar President and COO Tom Carter maintains an optimistic outlook for the future of pay-TV, predicting continued revenue flow rather than a sharp decline. He acknowledges subscriber attrition but emphasizes that Nexstar doesn't foresee a "cliff" for bundled services, expecting a plateau given that a significant portion of older viewers still subscribe to pay-TV. Carter also noted that the FuboTV dispute represents a minor financial impact for Nexstar and Paramount, classifying it as a "CBS-only issue" driven by specific circumstances rather than a broad trend.

title: Comcast Targets Return to “Total” Media Business Profit Even Amid Peacock Losses
summary: Comcast aims to return its broader media business to profit growth despite anticipated peak losses of $3 billion for its Peacock streaming service in 2023. President Michael Cavanagh stated that they are focused on managing their media businesses to ensure overall profitability, acknowledging the shifting landscape of streaming and expressing satisfaction with Comcast's current asset portfolio. The company also remains open to future M&A if it aligns strategically and financially, and is preparing for a decision regarding its Hulu stake in early 2024.

title: The marketing tricks that have kept Barbie’s brand alive for over 60 years
summary: Barbie, despite initial rejection, has become one of America's most trusted brands, generating billions in sales and maintaining significant brand value over 60 years. Mattel has achieved this longevity through a "multiply" strategy, introducing supporting characters and storytelling, extending the brand into various product categories, and strategically targeting both young girls and older consumers with a sense of nostalgia. The brand has also faced and attempted to address criticism regarding unrealistic body standards and cultural commodification.

title: These Are All The Exciting New Thrills At Six Flags Theme Parks This Year
summary: Six Flags has announced new attractions and seasonal events coming to its parks across the U.S., Mexico, and Canada for the 2023 season. Highlights include new water park zones and interactive attractions at multiple locations, innovative roller coasters like the KID FLASH™ Cosmic Coaster, and the debut of unique experiences such as e-sports centers and rainforest trails. The article also details several seasonal events planned throughout the year, from "Scream Break" to "Holiday in the Park."

title: AT&T Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: AT&T Inc. (T) stock rose 0.60% to $18.43 on Friday, outperforming the broader market during a challenging trading session where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both fell. The stock broke a four-day losing streak but remained $3.10 below its 52-week high. AT&T also outperformed competitors like Netflix, Walt Disney Co., and Comcast.

title: Disney’s ‘The Little Mermaid’ Trailer Debuts During ‘The Oscars’
summary: During ABC's live broadcast of The Oscars, Disney stars Halle Bailey and Melissa McCarthy debuted the trailer for the live-action reimagining of "The Little Mermaid." The film is set to open exclusively in theaters on May 26, 2023. It tells the classic tale of Ariel, a spirited young mermaid who longs to experience the world beyond the sea and falls for Prince Eric, leading her to make a perilous deal with the sea witch Ursula.

title: Sonia Coleman Named Chief Human Resources Officer of The Walt Disney Company
summary: Sonia Coleman has been appointed Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer of The Walt Disney Company, effective April 8, 2023. She will report directly to CEO Robert A. Iger and be responsible for leading the company's human resources strategy and initiatives, succeeding Paul Richardson. Coleman previously led HR for Disney Entertainment and ESPN, bringing extensive experience in employee development, recruitment, and organizational leadership to her new role.

title: How a Disney books-and-records case blew up into culture war
summary: A Delaware Chancery Court case involving Walt Disney Co and shareholder Kenneth Simeone, initially a routine books-and-records lawsuit, has evolved into a culture war debate. Simeone, allegedly backed by the Thomas More Society, seeks internal documents on Disney's stance against Florida's "Don't Say Gay" bill, arguing it harmed the company. Disney contends the lawsuit is orchestrated to fish for culture-war ammunition rather than genuine shareholder interests.

title: MLBN and Apple TV+ national broadcasts to show Zoom Replay Operations Center live under new deal
summary: Major League Baseball (MLB) and Zoom Video Communications (NASDAQ: ZM) have announced a new partnership that will enhance the fan viewership experience by showing the Zoom Replay Operations Center live on MLB Network and Apple TV+ national broadcasts. This collaboration aims to create a more transparent replay review process, allowing fans to see the decision-making in action and hear from expert rules analysts. Beyond broadcasts, the deal also includes standardizing replay reviews with Zoom technology for on-field umpires and broader league-wide Zoom integration for secure information transmission, including the MLB Draft.

title: Royal Caribbean Group stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Royal Caribbean Group (RCL) stock surged 4.53% to $64.87, outperforming competitors like Walt Disney Co. (DIS) and Carnival Corp. (CCL) on a day of strong market performance. The company's shares closed below its 52-week high, but trading volume for the day exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Givinga Appoints Drew St. Germain as Chief Operating Officer
summary: Givinga, a philanthropic technology company based in Boston, has appointed Drew St. Germain as its first Chief Operating Officer. St. Germain, who previously served on the executive team at InfoArmor and facilitated its sale to Allstate Identity Corporation, will lead Givinga's operational core platform and system integrations to support the company's next phase of growth. He is known for building strong operational teams and customer value, and is also involved in volunteer work with Habitat for Humanity and co-founded a nonprofit focused on carbon sequestration.

title: Salesforce avoids proxy fight with Elliott after improved results
summary: Salesforce Inc. and activist investor Elliott Management have reached an agreement where Elliott will not pursue a board challenge, following Salesforce's improved financial results and commitment to boosting profits and efficiency. Salesforce agreed to double its share buybacks to $20 billion and reduce acquisitions, satisfying Elliott and avoiding a costly proxy contest. This resolution is part of a trend among prominent activist investors, with similar withdrawals seen at Disney and Bath & Body Works.

title: Disney Begins the First Round of 7,000 Expected Job Cuts
summary: Walt Disney Co. has initiated the first phase of its planned 7,000 job cuts, a move designed to achieve $5.5 billion in savings. CEO Bob Iger announced that employees will be notified over the next four days, with further rounds of layoffs expected in April and before the summer. This marks a significant restructuring effort for the company.

title: The Walt Disney Co. will reportedly begin layoffs this week
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is set to begin its first round of layoffs this week, impacting employees as part of a larger plan to cut 7,000 jobs by summer. CEO Bob Iger stated that notifications would occur in three rounds, with the goal of saving $5.5 billion for the company. These job reductions follow a difficult period for Disney and align with recent layoffs seen across various industries.

title: XFL, The Walt Disney Company Celebrate Women’s History Month
summary: The XFL and The Walt Disney Company are celebrating Women's History Month by highlighting the partnership between the XFL, ESPN, and Disney. This article features Dany Garcia, Chairwoman and Owner of the XFL, and Rita Ferro, President of Disney Advertising, discussing their collaboration and its implications for advertising and new football fans. They also touched upon navigating a male-dominated industry and their excitement for this monumental partnership.

title: Lionsgate Takes Key Step In Separation Of Studio & Starz
summary: Lionsgate has confidentially submitted a draft registration for the proposed spinoff of its studio business from Starz to the SEC, aiming for completion by the quarter ending in September. This move is intended to unlock value for the company, as Wall Street has anticipated the transaction for over a year. The separation will allow both the studio and Starz to operate as distinct entities, potentially enhancing their respective market values and strategic flexibility.

title: Marvel Studios Shares ‘Secret Invasion’ Trailer and Premiere Date
summary: Marvel Studios has released the trailer for its new espionage thriller series, "Secret Invasion," which will premiere on Disney+ on June 21. The series, set in the present-day MCU, features Nick Fury and his allies in a race against time to prevent a clandestine invasion of Earth by shapeshifting Skrulls. The show boasts a star-studded cast including Samuel L. Jackson, Ben Mendelsohn, Emilia Clarke, Olivia Colman, and Don Cheadle.

title: CBS Affiliates Finally Return to Fubo
summary: More than 200 local CBS affiliate stations have returned to Fubo after a two-month dispute stemming from the CBS Affiliate Board's rejection of Paramount Global's revised retransmission agreement for live-streamed pay TV services. This resolution follows station groups like Sinclair and Nexstar pulling their CBS affiliates from Fubo, highlighting a broader push by local station owners to control their own retrans negotiations with vMVPDs. The issue underscores the growing tension between networks and their affiliates over digital distribution rights.

title: Dwayne Johnson Reveals Plans for Live-Action Reimagining of Disney’s ‘Moana’
summary: Dwayne Johnson announced that a live-action reimagining of Disney's "Moana" is in development, with Johnson, Dany Garcia, and Hiram Garcia producing. The project will celebrate Pacific Islander culture, similar to the original animated film. Johnson expressed deep personal connection to the story and culture, while Auli‘i Cravalho, the original voice of Moana, will serve as an executive producer and anticipates sharing the story in a new way.

title: Former President of Worldwide Operations of Walt Disney Parks and Resorts Al Weiss Has Joined SKYX as a Senior Business Development Advisor
summary: Al Weiss, former President of Worldwide Operations of Walt Disney Parks and Resorts, has joined SKYX Platforms Corp. as a senior business development advisor. He will help SKYX with strategic business introductions, partnerships, and engagements globally. Weiss brings a 39-year career at Disney, including overseeing worldwide amusement parks and resorts, and believes SKYX's smart platform technologies will become a new standard for safety and smart features in various buildings.

title: Asad Ayaz Named The Walt Disney Company’s First-Ever Chief Brand Officer
summary: Asad Ayaz has been appointed as The Walt Disney Company's first-ever Chief Brand Officer, effective immediately, reporting to CEO Robert A. Iger. In this new global role, Ayaz will be responsible for enhancing the Disney brand while continuing his duties as President of Marketing for The Walt Disney Studios. He will oversee comprehensive brand marketing campaigns, digital and social media strategy, and crucial initiatives like the Disney100 celebration.

title: ‘Avatar: The Way of Water’ Top-Selling Movie in the U.K. Year-to-Date
summary: Twentieth Century Studios' 'Avatar: The Way of Water' rapidly became the top-selling movie in the U.K. home entertainment market for 2023, achieving over 160,000 digital downloads in its first week. This performance marks the biggest first-week sales since 'Top Gun: Maverick' in August 2022. Other notable entries in the U.K. chart include 'Roald Dahl’s Matilda the Musical' at No. 2 and 'Elvis' at No. 3.

title: Undervalued Communication Services Stocks
summary: This article identifies undervalued communication services stocks, highlighting names like Comcast, Disney, and Alphabet, which are trading at discounts after a challenging 2022. It screens for companies within the Morningstar US Communication Services Index that have a 4 or 5-star Morningstar Rating and a wide economic moat, providing analyst insights for the top five. The communication services sector saw a significant rebound in early 2023 after substantial losses in the previous year.

title: AMC boosted by rebound in foot traffic and Gen Z visits, research finds
summary: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Cinemark Holdings, and Regal Cinemas are experiencing a significant rebound in cinema attendance, driven by increased foot traffic and visits from Gen Z. Research from Placer.ai indicates that attendance in February 2023 was over 322% higher than in January 2021, when the industry was grappling with pandemic-related disruptions. This resurgence highlights a positive trend for movie theater chains.

title: Kroger Makes a Big Retail Media Deal With Disney
summary: Kroger Precision Marketing has partnered with Disney Advertising to share first-party shopper data for targeting streaming audiences on Hulu. This collaboration aims to provide advertisers with advanced targeting and measurement capabilities, allowing them to reach consumers more effectively and measure sales impact across Kroger stores. PepsiCo was the first advertiser to test this new solution, which is expected to be available to other brands in the second half of 2023.

title: B+C Hall of Fame 2023: Matt Bond
summary: Matt Bond, Chairman of Content Distribution at NBCUniversal, is honored by the B+C Hall of Fame for his influential career in cable programming and distribution. Known as a tough negotiator from his time at TCI and Comcast to his current role at NBCU, Bond has been involved in numerous significant transactions. The article also highlights his remarkable recovery from a severe heart attack and his philosophical view of his career journey from the "Model T era" to the "Tesla era" of television.

title: JAKKS Pacific Reveals New Line of Toys Inspired by Disney’s ‘The Little Mermaid’
summary: JAKKS Pacific has unveiled a new line of toys, including dolls, role-play items, and dress-up costumes, inspired by Disney's upcoming film "The Little Mermaid." The collection features an "Under the Sea Exploring Ariel Doll" that sings and lights up, an Ariel-inspired fashion dress, a "Found Treasures Set," a "Singing Seashell Necklace," and "King Triton's All-Powerful Trident." These toys are designed to coincide with the movie's release on May 26, 2023, offering fans various ways to engage with the film's characters and story.

title: Disney Begins Largest Wave Of Layoffs, Will Get More Than Halfway To Target Of 7,000 Staff Cuts This Week
summary: Disney is implementing the second and largest phase of its planned layoffs, aiming to cut 4,000 of its targeted 7,000 staff by Thursday. The company expects these reductions, along with other austerity measures, to achieve $5.5 billion in cost savings. These layoffs, which do not include frontline theme park workers, are part of CEO Bob Iger's strategy to address the decline in pay-TV revenue and continued losses in streaming services.

title: Disney cuts thousands of jobs in second wave of layoffs | Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company has begun a second wave of layoffs, aiming to eliminate 7,000 positions and save $5.5 billion in costs across its business segments, including ESPN and Disney Parks. This round will cut several thousand jobs, bringing the total reductions to 4,000, with a third round expected before summer. The company's goal is to streamline its operations and prioritize profitability following a shift in the entertainment industry's focus from subscriber growth.

title: ¿Quién es el dueño de IZZI, la empresa de telecomunicaciones?
summary: This article details the ownership and services of IZZI, a telecommunications company. It highlights that Grupo Televisa, led by the Emilio Azcárraga Jean family, is the owner of IZZI. The piece also covers IZZI's range of services, including internet, telephony, and television, its recent expansion into mobile virtual network operations, and its price adjustments due to inflation.

title: Special Screens, Effects Draw More Movie Viewers
summary: Filmmakers and cinema operators are attracting moviegoers with special screens and effects, an effort to boost attendance which is still 16% below 2019 levels for American and Canadian ticket sales. Premium viewing experiences, such as IMAX and large format screens with immersive sound and moving seats, are becoming increasingly popular, accounting for a growing percentage of ticket sales and multiplex profits. Industry leaders report a rise in global interest for these enhanced cinematic experiences, especially for action and effects-filled films.

title: VFX Software Market May See A Big Move | Major Giants Autodesk, Boris FX, Milk VFX
summary: A new research publication by Advance Market Analytics highlights significant growth opportunities in the VFX Software Market, driven by increasing R&D spending and demand for visual effects in film and entertainment. Key players include Adobe, Autodesk, and The Walt Disney Company, with current trends pointing to the adoption of A.I. and cloud-based technologies. The report details market segmentation by application, enterprise size, industry vertical, and deployment, projecting continued expansion due to evolving digital content demands.

title: Disney+ sheds 4 million subscribers. Iger plans ‘one app experience’ with Hulu shows
summary: Disney+ experienced a significant subscriber loss of 4 million, primarily due to the performance of its low-cost Disney+ Hotstar service in India, marking its second consecutive quarterly decline. Despite this, Disney's streaming division narrowed its financial losses, and CEO Bob Iger announced plans for a "one app experience" integrating Hulu content with Disney+ for domestic subscribers. The company is undergoing major cost-cutting efforts, including job eliminations and a critical reassessment of content production for streaming, aiming for profitability by the end of fiscal 2024.

title: Falcon's Beyond Announces Robust Fan Engagement with Recently Launched Roblox Experience
summary: Falcon's Beyond announced strong fan engagement for its recently launched BEYONDLAND experience on Roblox, attracting over two million visits and a 93% positive approval rating since March. BEYONDLAND, designed as a virtual theme park, features various games and attractions, including a reimagining of the company's Katmandu Park. This success reinforces Falcon's strategy to expand its intellectual properties across physical and virtual entertainment platforms.

title: George Soros bet on railroads, fitness, gig economy and lightened load on Disney, Amazon, dumped Tesla
summary: Soros Fund Management made new investments in railroad operators CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp., and the gig economy during the first quarter. The fund also adjusted its holdings in the media sector and divested from electric-vehicle maker Tesla Inc. These railroad investments occurred amidst ongoing labor tensions and increased scrutiny over safety in the industry.

title: The Walt Disney Co. nixes massive $1B Lake Nona campus in Orlando
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has canceled its plans to build a $1 billion campus in Orlando's Lake Nona community, citing "changing business conditions." This decision impacts thousands of jobs expected to relocate and comes amid ongoing disputes between Disney and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis. The projected investment was substantial, and the cancellation marks a significant shift in Disney's regional development strategy.

title: Opinion: How “Willow” Has Eroded My Faith in the Walt Disney Company as Lucasfilm’s Caretaker
summary: The author expresses disappointment in The Walt Disney Company's handling of Lucasfilm content, specifically the cancellation and removal of the "Willow" series from Disney+. This action, along with similar removals of other Disney+ originals, is seen as a short-sighted financial decision that discourages creatives and limits public access to content. The author argues that Disney should at least make these removed series available for purchase on physical or digital media to respect both the creators and the fans.

title: Steve Jobs: Apple Cofounder and Tech Innovator
summary: Steve Jobs, co-founder of Apple Inc., was an American inventor, designer, and entrepreneur responsible for pioneering revolutionary technologies like the iPhone and iPad. The article details his life from adoption and early education to co-founding Apple, his departure and subsequent ventures with NeXT and Pixar, and his triumphant return to Apple, ultimately shaping modern technology. It also covers his personal life, battle with pancreatic cancer, and lasting legacy after his death in 2011.

title: Disney doesn't want to build smaller theme parks as Universal forges ahead on new projects
summary: Disney's parks leader, Josh D'Amaro, stated that the company is not interested in building smaller regional theme parks, distinguishing its strategy from Universal. Instead, Disney will focus on investing in its core assets and leveraging its strong intellectual properties like Marvel, Star Wars, and Mickey Mouse for new theme park experiences. D'Amaro also addressed decisions regarding the Star Wars hotel and the Imagineers' move to Lake Nona during an investor conference.

title: ‘World of Barbie' Experience Extends Its SoCal Run
summary: The "World of Barbie" immersive experience, which opened its U.S. debut in Santa Monica last month, has extended its run through September 4 due to popular demand. The attraction, spanning 20,000 square feet, allows fans to explore a life-sized Dreamhouse, engage with various Barbie careers, and interact with a Barbie Camper Van. Special events like "Pink Carpet Night," "Movie Days," and "Sips After Sunset" will also be held.

title: Right-wing investment fund dumps Target stock over ‘woke’ agenda, adds retailer to ‘refuse to buy’ list
summary: The American Conservative Values ETF (ACVF) has divested its holdings in Target Corp. and added the retailer to its "Refuse to Buy" list, citing the company's "woke" agenda and its handling of Pride merchandising. ACVF criticized Target's "ever-increasing pandering to the Woke LGBT agenda," stating that it has damaged the brand and will likely harm its long-term stock performance. This move comes as Target faces backlash from both conservatives and liberals regarding its LGBTQ+ merchandise displays and subsequent actions.

title: Anti-ESG Shareholder Proposals in 2023
summary: This article discusses the increasing volume and persistent low support for anti-ESG shareholder proposals in 2023, primarily focusing on social policy issues like diversity and corporate political involvement rather than environmental concerns. It details the various proponents, including think tanks and investment groups, and examines the outcomes and themes of their proposals across areas such as human rights, diversity, liberal bias, gun control, political influence, and environmental issues. Despite a surge in the number of proposals, most receive minimal investor backing, often below the threshold for resubmission.

title: Verizon offers exclusive savings via myPlan perks and first-of-its-kind streaming bundle on +play
summary: Verizon is introducing an exclusive streaming bundle on its +play platform, offering Netflix's Premium Plan and the Paramount+ with SHOWTIME bundle together for $25.99, saving customers $70 annually. This industry-first bundle is available only to Verizon customers and can be further discounted through myPlan's +play monthly credit perk. The initiative aims to provide unique value and simplify subscription management for users.

title: Outlets at Tejon holding Disneyland sweepstakes throughout June
summary: The Outlets at Tejon will host a Disneyland sweepstakes throughout June, starting on June 9th. Four winners will each receive four tickets to Disneyland. Participants can enter daily, with additional entries for shopping receipts from any outlet retailer, limited to five entries per retailer.

title: New ETF claims to offer ‘convenient solution’ for investors looking for exposure to the global music industry
summary: A new Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF), the MUSQ Global Music Industry Index ETF, is launching to offer investors exposure to the global music industry. Developed by MUSQ LLC and tracking an index of 49 companies across various music segments, this ETF aims to provide a convenient investment solution. It joins a growing trend of themed ETFs, arriving as some major music companies like Spotify and SM Entertainment show strong stock performance, while others like Live Nation have seen declines.

title: NLPC Pushes Comcast to Disclose More About China Ties
summary: The National Legal and Policy Center (NLPC) presented a "Communist China Risk Audit" proposal at Comcast Corporation's annual shareholder meeting, urging the company to disclose its vulnerabilities related to its extensive business in China. NLPC Chairman Peter Flaherty highlighted three examples: Comcast's partnership in Universal Beijing Resort where the Chinese government holds majority ownership and imposed "Zero COVID" closures; Universal Pictures' concessions to the Chinese government for market access; and NBC's perceived capitulation to the Chinese Communist Party during the 2022 Beijing Olympics by downplaying human rights issues. The NLPC emphasizes the need for greater transparency regarding Comcast's operations in China for shareholders.

title: The World’s Largest Media Companies In 2023: Comcast And Disney Stay On Top
summary: Despite a tumultuous year, Walt Disney Co. (No. 87 on the Global 2000) remains the second-largest media company, holding its position behind Comcast (No. 51). Disney's year included the return of CEO Bob Iger, significant cost-cutting measures, and a legal battle with Florida, while streaming competitors like Netflix (No. 223) and Warner Bros. Discovery (No. 559) also made strategic changes in the competitive media landscape. Forbes' ranking is based on assets, market value, sales, and profit.

title: United Airlines to Sponsor Ryan Reynolds-Owned Wrexham Football Club
summary: United Airlines Holdings Inc. has announced a major sponsorship agreement with Wrexham AFC, the Welsh football club owned by actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney. This partnership follows Wrexham's promotion to the English Football League and will see United's logo featured on the team's shirts. The club's global profile has significantly risen since the Hollywood takeover in early 2021, boosted by a documentary series.

title: DeSantis’ Battle Against ‘WOKE’ Corporations: How Walt Disney Co. Became the Epicenter
summary: This article details the year-long dispute between Florida Governor Ron DeSantis and Walt Disney Co., sparked by DeSantis's efforts to regulate "WOKE" corporations through House Bill 9B. The conflict, centered around Disney's former Reedy Creek Improvement District, has led to lawsuits from both sides concerning constitutional rights and contract agreements. The outcome of these legal battles is significant for Florida's socio-political norms, tourist economy, and DeSantis's political future.

title: Disney and Pixar Unveil ‘Elio’ Teaser Trailer and Poster
summary: Disney and Pixar have released a teaser trailer and poster for their upcoming animated feature film, "Elio." The movie follows Elio, an imaginative underdog who is mistakenly identified as Earth's ambassador after being beamed up to an interplanetary organization called the Communiverse. He must navigate this new world, form alliances with eccentric aliens, and discover his true purpose.

title: Return of the SPAC? Entertainment and sports-focused ESH Acquisition Corp prices $100m IPO
summary: ESH Acquisition Corp, a Special Purpose Acquisition Company focused on entertainment and sports, has priced its IPO at $100 million, a third of its original target. The company, led by CEO James Francis and Chairperson Allen Weiss, aims to merge with businesses in the music, entertainment, sports, or hospitality sectors. This IPO comes amidst a decline in SPAC popularity following tightened SEC regulations, though several music companies previously used SPACs for market debuts.

title: Christine McCarthy to Step Down as Disney’s Chief Financial Officer; Kevin Lansberry to Assume Role to Interim CFO
summary: Christine McCarthy, Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of The Walt Disney Company, will step down from her role on July 1 to take a family medical leave of absence. Kevin Lansberry, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, will serve as the interim CFO. McCarthy will remain a strategic advisor to the company during the transition to a permanent successor.

title: Christine McCarthy To Step Down As Disney’s Chief Financial Officer; Kevin Lansberry Will Assume Role Of Interim CFO
summary: Christine McCarthy is stepping down as Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of The Walt Disney Company due to family medical leave. She will continue as a strategic advisor to ensure a smooth transition. Kevin Lansberry, Executive Vice President and CFO of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, will serve as interim CFO while a search for a permanent replacement is conducted.

title: Macau ops make progress on non-casino ents: scholar
summary: Macau's casino concessionaires are increasing their non-gaming entertainment offerings, driven by competition and government policy to attract families and younger consumers. Scholar Carlos Siu Lam notes a significant uptick in events, including concerts, although many are currently one-off or short runs. Operators are cautiously investing in popular Asian artists to ensure demand, learning from past failures of Western-style shows not appealing to Chinese preferences.

title: Maximum Effort Channel, a Partnership Between Fubo and Ryan Reynolds’ Maximum Effort, Will Launch on Fubo, Amazon Freevee, LG Channels, Plex, Sling Freestream, VIDAA, VIZIO WatchFree+, Xumo Play
summary: FuboTV Inc. and Ryan Reynolds’ Maximum Effort announced that the "Maximum Effort Channel" will launch on June 20, 2023, across multiple platforms including Fubo, Amazon Freevee, and Sling Freestream. The channel will feature original and classic TV and movies, kicking off with "Bedtime Stories with Ryan." This launch is part of a multi-year partnership between Fubo and Maximum Effort, with Maximum Effort having creative control over the channel's content.

title: What Does Logitech CEO’s Abrupt Departure Mean?
summary: Logitech's stock fell sharply following the immediate resignation of its CEO, Bracken Darrel, after ten years, raising investor uncertainty, especially since the company's CFO also resigned recently. The abrupt departure amid a turnaround attempt and declining financials, including a 22% revenue plunge, has led to a Citi downgrade to Neutral. The article explores possible reasons for the resignation, noting the lack of a pre-planned successor, and analyzes the stock's bear flag chart pattern, suggesting further downside.

title: Producer Ryan Murphy Is Expected to Move to Disney (Published 2023)
summary: Ryan Murphy, the megaproducer behind hits like "American Horror Story" and "Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story," is reportedly set to move his production operation to the Walt Disney Company after his $300 million Netflix deal expires. This move would reunite Murphy with Disney executives he previously worked with for over a decade, with whom he continued to produce shows even during his Netflix contract. The deal is still in negotiation and is not expected to be finalized until after the screenwriters' strike is resolved.

title: Can Barbie and the New MCU Rescue Mattel Stock?
summary: Mattel (NYSE: MAT) stock has underperformed the S&P 500 in 2023, but the upcoming Barbie movie and the expansion of its iconic IPs into a "Mattel Cinematic Universe" (MCU) could provide a significant boost. Despite a Q1 2023 slump in financials, with reduced sales and increased losses, the company reaffirmed its full-year guidance, suggesting a low bar for improvement. The success of the Barbie movie and future film projects based on Hot Wheels, Master of the Universe, and other brands are critical for turning around investor sentiment and improving Mattel's financial performance.

title: 6 Disney Vacation Club Resorts Named Best for Families by Travel + Leisure Readers
summary: Six Disney Vacation Club resorts have been recognized by Travel + Leisure readers as among the 15 Best U.S. Resorts for Families in 2022. The article highlights unique family-friendly features of each resort, including Aulani Resort in Hawai'i, Disney's Grand Californian Hotel & Spa, Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge, Disney's Beach Club Resort, Disney's Hilton Head Island Resort, and Disney's Vero Beach Resort. These resorts offer diverse experiences from Hawaiian culture and theme park access to wildlife viewing and sea turtle nesting programs, emphasizing their appeal for creating lasting family memories.

title: Cruise Market Size ( USD 22.8 Billion by 2032) with 11.5% CAGR | According To Market.us
summary: The cruise market is projected to reach USD 22.8 billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 11.5% from its 2022 valuation of USD 7.9 billion. This growth is driven by increasing consumer demand, affordable luxury options, and expanding middle-class and aging populations. While facing challenges like environmental concerns and geopolitical instability, the industry is seeing opportunities in emerging markets, expedition cruising, and multigenerational travel, with a focus on health, safety, and sustainable practices for future outlook.

title: A wrecking operation?: Warner Brothers Discovery initiates new round of layoffs, targets Turner Classic Movies
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) has initiated a new round of layoffs, primarily affecting its cable television networks, with a significant impact on Turner Classic Movies (TCM). This move follows a series of cost-cutting measures since the company's formation in April 2022, aimed at consolidating management and reducing debt. The changes at TCM, including leadership purges and budget cuts, have sparked criticism from prominent Hollywood filmmakers, raising concerns about the future of artistically driven programming amidst Wall Street pressures for increased profits in the entertainment industry.

title: Communication Services Stock Outlook: As Meta and Alphabet Soar, Traditional Telecom Comes Under Renewed Pressure
summary: This article discusses the contrasting performances within the communication services sector, highlighting the surge in Meta and Alphabet shares due to renewed online advertising demand and AI excitement. Conversely, traditional telecom companies like Verizon and AT&T face renewed pressure, though recent price increases and cost-cutting efforts are expected to improve their cash flow. The report also provides specific picks and fair value estimates for Disney, Verizon Communications, and Pinterest.

title: Royal Caribbean Group names Heather Hust Rivera global communications head
summary: Royal Caribbean Group has appointed Heather Hust Rivera as SVP and global chief communications officer, effective Monday. Hust Rivera joins from Disney, where she held various communications roles since 2005, most recently as SVP of communications for Disney’s media and entertainment distribution. She will be responsible for Royal Caribbean Group’s corporate reputation, global corporate communications, incident and crisis management, and executive and internal communications.

title: Movie theater sales results have been mixed so far in the 2023 summer blockbuster season
summary: The 2023 summer blockbuster season has seen mixed sales results for major movie theater chains like AMC, Cinemark, and Cineworld, despite high-profile premieres. While the opening week showed year-over-year sales decreases for all companies, Cinemark experienced a brief increase in the second week due to Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse. The analysis also highlights that AMC's sales per customer growth has outpaced customer count growth in recent weeks, a reversal from earlier in the year, attributed to premium formats, increased concessions, and tiered pricing.

title: Disney+ Shares New Trailer for ‘Star Wars: Ahsoka’
summary: Disney+ has released a new trailer for Lucasfilm’s Star Wars: Ahsoka, announcing that the series will premiere on Wednesday, August 23, with its first two episodes. The show, set after the fall of the Empire, features Rosario Dawson as Ahsoka Tano as she confronts a new threat to the galaxy. The series boasts a large cast, with episodes directed by multiple talents and Dave Filoni serving as head writer and executive producer.

title: Disney ramps up spending in California amid war with Ron DeSantis in Florida
summary: Disney is reportedly shifting its investment focus towards California and away from Florida amid its ongoing conflict with Florida Governor Ron DeSantis over LGBTQ+ rights. The company canceled a $1 billion project and a Star Wars hotel in Florida while committing to an ambitious growth program in Anaheim, California. Analysts and former executives suggest this strategic pivot is directly linked to the political dispute and Disney's desire to prioritize environments favorable to its employees and expansion plans.

title: Following the Women’s World Cup? You’re sure to see Ally Financial.
summary: Ally Financial, a prominent sponsor of women's sports and the NWSL, is increasing its presence at the FIFA Women's World Cup through broadcast ads on Fox Sports and other campaign platforms. The company is committed to its pledge of equally splitting ad spend between men's and women's sports within five years, aiming for a 60/40 split by the end of the current year. Despite challenges in securing media inventory, Ally has developed various activations, including collaborations with former USWNT player Julie Foudy, to amplify its World Cup involvement.

title: Media mogul Barry Diller says Hollywood executives, top actors should take 25% pay cut to end strikes
summary: Media mogul Barry Diller suggested that top Hollywood executives and highly paid actors should take a 25% pay cut to help bridge the divide between high and low earners during the ongoing writers' and actors' strikes. Diller warned that if the strikes continue until the end of the year, it could lead to an "absolute collapse" of the industry due to a lack of new programming and reduced revenue from subscriptions. He also expressed skepticism about the concerns over AI replacing creative roles, believing it will more likely assist rather than replace them.

title: Netflix Reports Blockbuster Earnings, as Password-Sharing Crackdown Leads to 5.9M New Subscribers
summary: Netflix reported strong Q2 2023 earnings, adding 5.9 million new paid subscribers, largely attributed to its password-sharing crackdown. The company is expanding this "paid sharing" strategy globally and is pushing its ad-supported plan by eliminating the cheapest ad-free option. Despite a soft advertising market, Netflix remains confident in its long-term revenue growth and ability to make its streaming service profitable.

title: Netflix Strategic Changes Led to User Base Expansion & Record Revenues in Q2 2023
summary: Netflix's strategic changes, including a crackdown on password sharing and the introduction of an ad-supported tier, significantly boosted its user base and revenue in Q2 2023. The company added 5.89 million subscribers and achieved record revenues of $8.187 billion, demonstrating the positive impact of these initiatives despite increasing competition in the direct-to-consumer market. Even with these successes, challenges remain, such as intense competition and the absence of live sports content, which are critical for long-term growth and investor satisfaction.

title: Netflix falls as benefits from password-sharing crackdown to take time
summary: Netflix shares fell over 8% after its second-quarter revenue growth and forecast lagged estimates, despite adding nearly 6 million subscribers due to a password-sharing crackdown and new ad-supported tier. Executives cautioned that it would take "several quarters" to see significant returns from these new initiatives, leading to an $18 billion loss in market value. Analysts remain broadly optimistic, citing the potential for accelerated revenue growth in the latter half of 2023 and Netflix's strong content lineup amidst the Hollywood strike.

title: Disney Advertising and Ally Flip the Game with Women-Focused SportsCenter Takeovers on ESPN
summary: Disney Advertising and Ally Financial have partnered to launch two "SportsCenter" takeovers focused on women's sports. These takeovers, featuring an all-female production team and anchors Elle Duncan and Nicole Briscoe, are part of Ally's commitment to achieving equal advertising spending on women's and men's sports by 2027. The initiative aims to increase visibility and investment in women's sports through unique content and commercial messaging.

title: Pixar, Apple and Nvidia are teaming up to promote a 3D file format that could help boost Apple's upcoming Vision Pro
summary: Pixar, Apple, Nvidia, Adobe, and Autodesk are collaborating to promote OpenUSD, a 3D file format. This initiative aims to streamline the creation of 3D content, potentially benefiting game development based on Pixar movies and boosting Apple's upcoming Vision Pro mixed-reality headset by making 3D environments more accessible.

title: Charter Communications To Cover College Tuition For Full-Time Workers
summary: Charter Communications announced a new Education Benefit in partnership with Guild, offering to cover 100% of tuition costs for full-time employees pursuing select college degrees and short-term certificates. This program, available to over 101,000 employees from their first day, includes access to more than 300 online programs from various universities and also covers up to $10,000 annually for graduate degrees outside the Guild catalog, along with program-related expenses. The initiative aims to provide career mobility, enhance workforce knowledge, and benefit customers.

title: 2 Consumer Stocks That Could Echo Mattel’s Barbie Movie Success
summary: Following the success of the Barbie movie, this article identifies two undervalued consumer companies, Hasbro and Kellogg, with strong brand-driven economic moats that could replicate Mattel's success through well-executed media extensions. It emphasizes the importance of intangible assets, effective execution in bridging the digital divide, and sound valuation for successful investments in this space.

title: Disney Celebrates the Wonder of Disney Princess with New Products and Collaborations
summary: Disney is celebrating its 100th anniversary by highlighting the iconic Disney Princess brand throughout August, leading up to World Princess Week (August 20-26). New products and collaborations are launching, including a LEGO castle, a four-foot-tall Disney Princess Magical Adventures Castle from Mattel, and a Gourmet Cook N’ Care Kitchen from JAKKS Pacific. Other releases feature dress-up apparel, beauty products, Loungefly accessories, Corkcicle drinkware, Funko POPs, and limited-edition American Girl dolls and Mattel Creations collector dolls.

title: Top stock reports to watch this week (07.08.2023)
summary: This article lists the top U.S. companies scheduled to report their Q2 financial results during the week of August 7, 2023. These include well-known companies like Palantir, Lyft, Take-Two Interactive, and Walt Disney. Although most large U.S. companies have already reported, the earnings season continues with these smaller but significant reports.

title: Barstool Sportsbook to be rebranded ESPN Bet in fall
summary: ESPN is partnering with PENN Entertainment to launch ESPN Bet, a new online sports betting platform set to replace Barstool Sportsbook this fall. PENN Entertainment sold Barstool Sports back to Dave Portnoy. The agreement involves PENN paying ESPN $1.5 billion over an initial 10-year term.

title: Mickey Mouse Piccadilly Paisley Collection by Vera Bradley Arrives on shopDisney
summary: Vera Bradley is launching its Mickey Mouse Piccadilly Paisley Collection on shopDisney, featuring travel accessories with Mickey, Minnie, Pluto, and Figaro. The collection includes totes, purses, and backpacks with prices ranging from $45-$160. Items will be available starting August 10th, with a colorful design set against a light grey background.

title: Campbell Soup, Disney partner on LTO product
summary: Campbell Soup Company has partnered with The Disney Co. to release limited-edition soup and snack products commemorating Disney's 100th anniversary. These products include Goldfish crackers featuring Disney characters and special packaging for Campbell's tomato and Disney Princess soups. This collaboration follows a similar partnership between Disney and Post Consumer Brands earlier in the year.

title: Top Analyst Reports for Procter & Gamble, AbbVie & Walt Disney
summary: This article summarizes top analyst reports from Zacks Research Daily on Procter & Gamble (PG), AbbVie (ABBV), and The Walt Disney Company (DIS). It details the financial performance, challenges, and growth prospects for each company, highlighting key drivers and headwinds. Additionally, it mentions other noteworthy reports on HSBC, Boston Scientific, and Duke Energy.

title: YieldMax Launches Option Income Strategy ETFs on Microsoft and Disney
summary: YieldMax has introduced two new active ETFs, the YieldMax MSFT Option Income Strategy ETF (MSFO) and the YieldMax DIS Option Income Strategy ETF (DISO), designed to generate monthly income through a synthetic covered call strategy on Microsoft and Disney stocks, respectively. These new ETFs, actively managed by ZEGA Financial, join a growing suite of YieldMax products that employ similar strategies on other major companies like Coinbase, Netflix, Meta Platforms, Alphabet, and Amazon.

title: Behind the Deal: Manhattan’s First Purpose-Built Film and TV Studio Campus
summary: Blackstone, along with Vornado Realty Trust and Hudson Pacific Properties, is developing Manhattan's first purpose-built film and TV studio campus at Pier 94. This approximately $350 million investment, known as Sunset Pier 94 Studios, will feature six state-of-the-art soundstages and capitalize on the growing demand for content creation and New York State's increased film tax credits. The project is a public-private partnership with the NYCEDC and aims to contribute millions annually to the local economy while providing much-needed modern studio infrastructure in a prime Manhattan location.

title: New ZEGA ETFs Let Investors Play Disney and Microsoft on Easy Mode
summary: ZEGA Financial has expanded its YieldMax offerings by launching two new covered call ETFs: YieldMax MSFT Option Income Strategy ETF (MSFO) and YieldMax DIS Option Income Strategy ETF (DISO). These funds employ a synthetic covered call strategy on Microsoft and Disney stocks, aiming to provide monthly income and capital appreciation for investors seeking defensive positions in tech stocks. The ETFs allow for capped participation in price gains and are part of a trend of investors flocking to covered call funds amid a cautious market recovery.

title: Prudential Signs New Multi-Year Agreement with Disney Advertising as Presenting Sponsor of Historic Rose Bowl Game Through 2025-26
summary: Prudential Financial has extended its partnership with Disney Advertising and the Tournament of Roses, serving as the presenting sponsor of the Rose Bowl Game through the 2025-26 college football season. This multi-year agreement includes the 110th Rose Bowl Game in 2024 and subsequent games, with the 2024 game hosting a College Football Playoff Semifinal. Prudential will also be the official sponsor of the Pasadena Tournament of Roses, securing category exclusivity in life insurance, wealth management, and financial advisory.

title: The Fishbowl: Lydia Parker, Samsung Ads Europe
summary: This article features an interview with Lydia Parker, Head of International Agencies at Samsung Ads Europe, as part of The Media Leader's "Fishbowl" series. She discusses her career progression, professional experiences, leadership strategies in a hybrid work environment, changes in client conversations due to the booming CTV market, and her favorite ad.

title: Is a Wide Moat Better Than a Well-Managed Company? Here’s What the Data Says.
summary: Morningstar research suggests that investing in companies with a wide economic moat tends to lead to better stock performance than investing in companies with exemplary management but no moat. While strong management is desirable, durable competitive advantages prove more crucial for long-term returns. The article also discusses the mixed impact of acquisitions on a company's moat and the implications of dual share classes.

title: The Art of Restoring 27 Classic Walt Disney Animation Studios Shorts
summary: Disney+ is releasing 27 newly restored Walt Disney Animation Studios shorts, a project spearheaded by the Walt Disney Studios Restoration and Preservation team for the studio's centennial. Karen Weissman, Restoration and Preservation Manager, discusses the intricate process of restoring these films, including overcoming challenges like missing original elements and tracking down lost title cards. The team focused on preserving historical accuracy while making these classics accessible to new audiences.

title: Disney Parks unveils future projects, surprises at Destination D23
summary: During Destination D23 in Orlando, Florida, Disney Parks announced several new projects and updates.
